meta.purpose: Feature map of the Obsidian calendar / periodic-notes family, built to merge them into the obsidian-calendaric plugin.

sources.role: Shared library that resolves, creates and looks up periodic (daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/yearly) notes; used by obsidian-calendar-plugin and, historically, obsidian-periodic-notes.
Svelte component library rendering the calendar grid (month/week/day cells, nav, popover). Published as an npm package and consumed by obsidian-calendar-plugin.

Sidebar Calendar view: renders obsidian-calendar-ui, wired to obsidian-daily-notes-interface for daily/weekly note IO. Personal fork of matisnape/obsidian-calendar-plugin, branch master, HEAD 39040cd, 7 commits ahead of upstream/master.

Obsidian plugin: define one or more named 'calendar sets', each enabling day/week/month/quarter/year granularities with its own format/folder/template, create-or-open notes for those granularities, index existing notes into a cache, and expose a small API (openPeriodicNote, calendarSetManager, settings) for other plugins such as obsidian-calendar-plugin. Personal fork matisnape/obsidian-periodic-notes, branch main, HEAD e332ac6, installed in this vault under dev plugin id periodic-notes-anks.

MERGE TARGET. From-scratch rewrite started from the Obsidian sample plugin; intended to absorb the Calendar and Periodic Notes plugins into one repo. Plain TypeScript with hand-rolled DOM (no Svelte). Three feature commits so far: calendar view, settings view, create/open daily+weekly notes.
Real-world usage layer: the live Obsidian vault that consumes calendar/periodic-notes/templater. Shows which plugin features are actually depended on vs merely available.

sources.version: calendar-plugin 1.5.10 / periodic-notes 0.0.17 / daily-notes-interface 0.9.4 / calendar-ui local checkout 0.4.0 (but the plugin actually consumes published 0.3.12 -- see observations)

capabilities.name: Create a daily note
capabilities.description: Creates a new daily note file for a given Moment: resolves settings, applies the configured template (with fold state), fills in filename/date/time tokens, writes the file via vault.create, and returns the created TFile.
behaviour_notes: Mimics the core daily-notes plugin's mustache replacement so behavior stays in sync.
Restores Obsidian fold state on the new file via app.foldManager.save(createdFile, IFoldInfo) (src/daily.ts:65).
Does not check for an existing file before calling vault.create; relies on vault.create throwing.

On any failure (including 'file already exists'), logs to console, shows a generic Notice('Unable to create new file.'), and the function resolves to undefined instead of rejecting or returning null (src/daily.ts:68-71).
edge_cases: shows error if file creation failed (src/__tests__/daily.spec.ts pattern shared across granularities)
replaces all mustaches in template, including {{date+1d:format}}-style calc tokens

capabilities.name: Look up a daily note by date
capabilities.description: Given a Moment and a Record<dateUID, TFile> (as produced by getAllDailyNotes), returns the matching TFile or null.
behaviour_notes: Pure lookup keyed by getDateUID(date, 'day'); does not touch the vault itself.
Because getDateUID calls date.clone().startOf('day'), time-of-day differences on the lookup Moment do not affect the match.
edge_cases: returns note on the same day even if the HH:MM:SS is different
returns null if there is no daily note for a given date

capabilities.name: Enumerate all daily notes
capabilities.description: Recursively walks the configured daily-notes folder and returns a Record<dateUID, TFile> for every file whose name parses as a valid daily-note date.

capabilities.name: Parse a note's date from its filename
capabilities.description: Given a TFile (getDateFromFile) or a path string (getDateFromPath) plus a granularity, resolves that granularity's format and parses the basename into a Moment, first strictly, then (only if allowPrefixMatch is set) via loose/prefix matching. Returns null if nothing matches.
behaviour_notes: format is taken as settings.format.split('/').pop() — only the last path segment of the configured format is used for parsing (handles formats with folder-like separators).
Step 1: strict moment(filename, format, true). If valid, checked for 'ambiguity' (see below); returned as-is otherwise.

isFormatAmbiguous (src/parse.ts:36-45) only fires for granularity==='week' when the (bracket-stripped) format contains a week-number token (w/ww) AND also a month (M) or day (D) token. In that case the date is re-parsed non-strictly with M/D tokens stripped from the format, because moment prioritizes month+day over week-number when both are present, which is wrong for a week-numbered filename.
Step 2 (only if strict parse failed): if allowPrefixMatch is falsy, returns null immediately.

Step 2b: otherwise re-parses non-strictly, then re-formats the parsed moment with the same format and requires filename.startsWith(formattedDate) before accepting — this lets a filename with a descriptive suffix (e.g. '2025-W46, 10.11 - 16.11') still resolve to the same date as the strict prefix.

allowPrefixMatch only ever comes from resolve-weekly-settings (Periodic Notes weekly settings); the other four resolve-*-settings functions never set it, so day/month/quarter/year notes can never use prefix matching in this codebase even though the code path is generic.
edge_cases: it supports formats with year, month, and day

it supports formats with year and week number

capabilities.name: Resolve per-day/week/month metadata from registered sources
capabilities.description: PeriodicNotesCache.getEvaluatedMetadata(granularity, date, getSourceSettings) looks up the existing periodic note file for that date/granularity, calls `source.getMetadata?.(granularity, date, file)` for every registered ICalendarSource, and merges each result with the source's own id/name/description and its per-source display settings (color, display, order) into one IDayMetadata per source. capabilities.name: Configure global moment locale and week start
capabilities.description: configureGlobalMomentLocale(localeOverride, weekStart) resolves a moment locale from Obsidian's stored UI language (localStorage 'language'), an optional explicit override, or a more-specific system locale, applies it via `window.moment.locale(...)`, then overrides the locale's week-start day (or restores the original bundled week spec when weekStart is 'locale').
behaviour_notes: Caches the locale's original week spec on `window._bundledLocaleWeekSpec` the first time it runs, so later 'locale' selections restore the true bundled default rather than whatever was last forced.

This function is the ONLY mechanism that actually controls week start / weekday-name locale for the whole calendar — the `localeData` prop threaded through the components does not (see compute-month-grid behaviour_notes).

`weekdays.indexOf(weekStart) || 0` has a latent bug: indexOf returns 0 both for 'sunday' (correct, index 0) and for 'not found' (-1 would be truthy... actually -1 is truthy so `|| 0` only fires for exactly 0, i.e. 'sunday' silently falls back to dow 0 anyway by coincidence, but any genuinely invalid weekStart string produces dow -1, not a safe default).

It is hidden (checkCallback returns false) whenever Periodic Notes has weekly notes enabled, since Periodic Notes then owns that job. On invoke it delegates to the view's openOrCreateWeeklyNote for today, opened in the current leaf.
edge_cases: Command is unavailable via checkCallback, not just disabled -- it will not appear in the palette at all when Periodic Notes weekly is on.

capabilities.name: Reveal active note (command)
capabilities.description: Registers the 'reveal-active-note' command, always available; calls view.revealActiveNote() which jumps the calendar's displayed month to the currently open file's date.

capabilities.name: Load and persist plugin settings
capabilities.description: loadOptions() merges saved data.json into the `settings` Svelte store defaults on load and immediately re-saves; writeOptions() applies a partial patch to the store and re-saves data.json. The plugin also mirrors the live store value into `this.options` via a subscription so synchronous reads (e.g. settings.ts's `this.plugin.options`) stay current.
behaviour_notes: saveData() is called unconditionally after every loadOptions(), even if nothing changed, so a fresh install writes a data.json immediately.

capabilities.name: Mount the Svelte calendar into the view
capabilities.description: On ItemView.onOpen(), builds the built-in sources array (streak, tags, wordCount, tasks), fires the 'calendar:open' extension event with it, then instantiates the Calendar.svelte component into contentEl with click/hover/context-menu callbacks and the sources array as props.
behaviour_notes: The sources array passed to Calendar is the SAME array object trigger()'d to listeners, so a plugin handling calendar:open can push() extra sources into it before the Calendar component reads props.sources.

capabilities.name: Third-party metadata source extension point
capabilities.description: Fires the workspace event 'calendar:open' (TRIGGER_ON_OPEN) with the mutable sources array right before mounting the Svelte component, letting other plugins register additional ICalendarSource implementations.
behaviour_notes: Only fires once per view open; a plugin that loads after the calendar view has already opened will miss this event unless the view is closed and reopened.

capabilities.name: Click a day: open or create its daily note
capabilities.description: Looks up the daily note for the clicked date via the dailyNotes store; if it exists, opens it (in a split if inNewSplit) preserving the vault's configured default view mode and marks it the active file. If missing, delegates to tryToCreateDailyNote.
behaviour_notes: Reads app.vault.getConfig('defaultViewMode') to open the existing file in the user's preferred edit/preview mode -- the weekly equivalent does not do this (see gap observation).

capabilities.name: Click the week number: open or create its weekly note
capabilities.description: Looks up the weekly note for the clicked date's week via the weeklyNotes store; if it exists, opens it (in a split if inNewSplit) and marks it active, then calls workspace.setActiveLeaf. If missing, delegates to tryToCreateWeeklyNote.
behaviour_notes: Unlike openOrCreateDailyNote, does not pass a `mode` to leaf.openFile (no defaultViewMode lookup) -- see gap observation.

capabilities.name: Create a new daily note (with optional confirmation)
capabilities.description: Computes the target filename from the daily note format, then either shows a ConfirmationModal (if shouldConfirmBeforeCreate) or creates the file immediately via obsidian-daily-notes-interface's createDailyNote(). On accept/immediate path, opens the new file (split or unpinned leaf) and invokes the caller's callback with the new TFile.
behaviour_notes: The 'Never mind' button just closes the modal -- no file is created and no callback fires.
edge_cases: If createDailyNote throws (e.g. folder/template misconfiguration in obsidian-daily-notes-interface), the error propagates unhandled from the async createFile closure.

capabilities.name: Create a new weekly note (with optional confirmation)
capabilities.description: Same pattern as the daily-note flow: computes filename from the weekly note format, optionally confirms via modal, creates via createWeeklyNote(), opens it, and invokes the callback.
edge_cases: Same unhandled-throw risk as the daily variant.

capabilities.name: Generic accept/cancel confirmation modal
capabilities.description: A reusable Obsidian Modal with a title, body text, a 'Never mind' (close) button and a CTA button that awaits an onAccept callback before closing.
edge_cases: If onAccept rejects, the modal never calls this.close() (no catch) -- the dialog would appear stuck.

capabilities.name: Hover a day/week cell with Cmd/Ctrl to preview the note
capabilities.description: When onHoverDay/onHoverWeek fire with isMetaPressed=true, looks up the note for that date and triggers Obsidian's native 'link-hover' popover pointing at the note's path (or undefined if none exists).
behaviour_notes: Without the meta/ctrl key the handler returns immediately and does nothing (no plain hover preview).
edge_cases: Still calls workspace.trigger('link-hover', ...) even when no note exists for that date, passing `note?.path` as undefined -- whatever the hover-preview consumer does with an undefined path is undocumented here.

capabilities.name: Right-click a day/week cell
capabilities.description: onContextMenuDay/onContextMenuWeek look up the note for the clicked date; if one exists, delegate to showFileMenu() at the click position. If no note exists, nothing is shown.
edge_cases: No menu at all for empty days/weeks -- there's no 'create note' entry from the context menu.

capabilities.name: Build and show the note's file context menu
capabilities.description: Creates an Obsidian Menu with a 'Delete' item (calls fileManager.promptForFileDeletion), then triggers the standard 'file-menu' workspace event (source: 'calendar-context-menu') so other plugins can append their own items before showing the menu at the given position.

capabilities.name: Click the month header to open/create that month's periodic note
capabilities.description: A capture-phase click listener on the whole view container intercepts clicks that land on 'h3.title' (the month header, e.g. 'Oct 2026'). If a Periodic Notes instance with monthly notes enabled can be resolved, it reads the currently displayed month from Calendar.svelte and calls periodicNotes.openPeriodicNote('month', displayedMonth, { inNewSplit: <meta/ctrl pressed> }), then prevents default and stops propagation so obsidian-calendar-ui's own bubble-phase reset-to-today handler does not also fire.
behaviour_notes: This is a LOCAL FORK feature (commit 5ed4307), not present upstream.
Registered in the capture phase specifically to win the race against obsidian-calendar-ui's bubble-phase 'h3.title' click listener (resetDisplayedMonth).
The nav's separate '.reset-button' dot calls the same resetDisplayedMonth but is a different DOM element, so it is unaffected by this interceptor.
isMetaPressed is a local re-implementation of an unexported helper in obsidian-calendar-ui, kept in sync manually.
edge_cases: If Periodic Notes can't be resolved (not installed, monthly disabled, fail-closed), the handler returns without calling preventDefault/stopPropagation, so the upstream reset-to-current-month click still fires normally.
If displayedMonth can't be read off Calendar.svelte (defensive guard against a future obsidian-calendar-ui internal change), logs a console.warn and also falls through to the default reset behavior.

capabilities.name: (Upstream) reset displayed month to today on header click
capabilities.description: obsidian-calendar-ui's own bubble-phase click listener on 'h3.title' resets the calendar's displayedMonth back to today. Still runs whenever month-header-click-open-monthly-note does not intercept and stop the event.

defined_in.notes: Lives in obsidian-calendar-ui, outside this source root.

behaviour_notes: Not part of this repo's source; behavior inferred from the fork's own code comments describing the race it must win.

capabilities.name: Detect whether Periodic Notes owns weekly notes
capabilities.description: appHasPeriodicNotesPluginLoaded() looks up the Periodic Notes plugin instance (dev id first, then production id) and returns whether its weekly notes are enabled, by reading `periodicNotes.settings?.weekly?.enabled`.
behaviour_notes: Plugin id probe order: 'periodic-notes-anks' (dev build) then 'periodic-notes' (community-store build) -- fixed to include the dev id in commit 7727890 after being missed by the earlier dev-id/prefix-match fix.
edge_cases: Reads `periodicNotes.settings` directly as if it were a plain object. Per the sibling function's own commit message (39040cd), `settings` on the live Periodic Notes plugin instance is actually a Svelte store (Writable<ISettings>), not a plain object -- so `.weekly?.enabled` here may always read undefined the same way the monthly check did before it was fixed. This path was not covered by that fix. See observation.

capabilities.name: Resolve the Periodic Notes plugin only when monthly notes are enabled
capabilities.description: getMonthlyNotesPeriodicNotesPlugin() finds the Periodic Notes plugin instance, then checks the live 'is monthly enabled' answer via calendarSetManager.getActiveGranularities().includes('month'), and finally checks openPeriodicNote is callable. Returns the plugin instance or null.
behaviour_notes: Exact probe order: (1) pluginManager.getPlugin('periodic-notes-anks') [dev plugin id] || (2) pluginManager.getPlugin('periodic-notes') [production id]. If neither is found -> return null.
If found: check `periodicNotes.calendarSetManager` exists and its `getActiveGranularities` is a function; call it and require the result to include 'month', else return null.

FAIL-CLOSED BRANCH: if calendarSetManager or getActiveGranularities is missing on this Periodic Notes build, the function CANNOT verify monthly is enabled, so it returns null rather than guessing -- preserving the old 'fall back to reset click handler' behavior instead of risking a call into openPeriodicNote/createPeriodicNote for a possibly-disabled or unconfigured granularity.
Finally checks `typeof periodicNotes.openPeriodicNote === 'function'` before returning the instance.
This replaced an earlier (buggy) direct read of `periodicNotes.settings.monthly` -- that field was always undefined because `settings` is a Svelte store, not a plain object (fixed in commit 39040cd).
edge_cases: Local fork feature (commits 5ed4307, 39040cd); depends on Periodic Notes' internal calendarSetManager API shape, which is not a documented public contract.

capabilities.name: Calendar settings tab
capabilities.description: Renders the plugin's settings tab: a Daily Notes warning banner (conditional), General Settings (words-per-dot, week start, confirm-before-create, show-week-number), conditionally-shown legacy Weekly Note settings, and Advanced (locale override).
behaviour_notes: Legacy Weekly Note Settings section (format/template/folder) is only shown when showWeeklyNote is on AND Periodic Notes is not already handling weekly notes; it carries a migration note pointing users at the Periodic Notes plugin.

capabilities.name: Warn when Daily Notes plugin is not enabled
capabilities.description: The settings tab shows a warning banner recommending the Daily Notes or Periodic Notes plugin whenever appHasDailyNotesPluginLoaded() (from obsidian-daily-notes-interface) returns false.

capabilities.name: Streak dot source: has-note class
capabilities.description: For a given day/week, looks up the note in the dailyNotes/weeklyNotes store (no vault I/O) and returns a 'has-note' CSS class if it exists; no dots.
behaviour_notes: Cheapest of the four sources: a store lookup, no file read.
Always enabled; no dedicated setting.

capabilities.name: Custom tags source: data-attributes from frontmatter
capabilities.description: Reads the note's cached frontmatter (metadataCache, no disk I/O) and parses its tags. Splits them into emoji vs. non-emoji tags: non-emoji tags become a space-joined 'data-tags' attribute, and the first emoji tag becomes 'data-emoji-tag'.
behaviour_notes: Cheap: uses the metadata cache, not a file read.
Only the FIRST emoji tag is surfaced (data-emoji-tag), any additional emoji tags on the note are dropped.
Always enabled; no dedicated setting.
edge_cases: Notes with no frontmatter/tags produce empty data-attributes, not an absent object.

capabilities.name: Tasks source: incomplete-checkbox dot
capabilities.description: Reads the full note body via vault.cachedRead and regex-counts incomplete checkboxes ('- [ ]' or '* [ ]'). Shows one unfilled 'task' dot if the count is nonzero.
behaviour_notes: More expensive than streak/tags: does a full cachedRead() of every note file visible in the grid (cached by Obsidian, but still a per-day read/regex scan).
Only ever renders ONE dot regardless of how many incomplete tasks exist.
Always enabled; no dedicated setting.

capabilities.name: Word count source: filled dots by length
capabilities.description: Reads the full note body via vault.cachedRead, counts words with a unicode-aware tokenizer, then divides by the wordsPerDot setting and clamps to 1-5 filled dots.
behaviour_notes: Effectively disabled (returns 0 dots) when wordsPerDot <= 0.
Same per-day cachedRead cost as the tasks source.
edge_cases: A note with 1 word still shows at least 1 dot (Math.floor(...) clamped to a minimum of 1, not 0, once wordCount > 0 -- actually clamp(floor(numDots),1,5), so even a very short note with any positive numDots below 1 rounds down to 0 then is clamped UP to 1).

capabilities.name: Refresh calendar on vault file create/delete/modify
capabilities.description: Listens to vault 'create', 'delete', and 'modify'. For files whose name matches the daily or weekly note date format, reindexes the corresponding store (dailyNotes/weeklyNotes) and forces a re-render via calendar.tick().
behaviour_notes: onFileCreated additionally guards on `this.app.workspace.layoutReady` and `this.calendar` being set (so it's a no-op during initial vault indexing before the view has mounted).
onFileDeleted/onFileModified do NOT check layoutReady.
onFileModified reindexes nothing -- it only ticks the calendar (so dot metadata like word count/tasks re-renders), since modifying an existing file doesn't change which dates have notes.
edge_cases: A rename is seen by Obsidian as delete+create, not a single 'rename' handler here, so both reindexes run.

capabilities.name: Refresh on Periodic Notes settings change
capabilities.description: Listens for the custom workspace event 'periodic-notes:settings-updated' (fired by the Periodic Notes plugin itself) and reindexes both dailyNotes and weeklyNotes stores plus updates the active-file highlight.
edge_cases: Untyped event: cast via `(<any>this.app.workspace).on(...)` since this event isn't part of Obsidian's typed API.

capabilities.name: Re-render calendar when plugin settings change
capabilities.description: The view subscribes to the `settings` store in its constructor; any settings change (e.g. user edits words-per-dot or toggles show-week-number in the settings tab) re-renders the calendar via calendar.tick().
behaviour_notes: Guarded by `if (this.calendar)` since this subscription fires once immediately on construction, before the Svelte component exists.

capabilities.name: Track the active file for calendar highlighting
capabilities.description: On workspace 'file-open', updateActiveFile() reads the active leaf's file (if it's a FileView) and pushes its date-UID into the `activeFile` store, then ticks the calendar so the corresponding cell gets `selectedId` highlighting in Calendar.svelte.
behaviour_notes: Guarded on `this.app.workspace.layoutReady` -- does nothing during initial startup file-open events.

capabilities.name: Jump the calendar to the active note's date
capabilities.description: revealActiveNote() checks whether the active leaf's file is a daily or weekly note (via getDateFromFile) and, if so, sets the calendar's displayedMonth to that date.
behaviour_notes: Fixed in commit 7727890: previously called `moment(filename, format, true)` inline for the weekly check -- a strict-only parse that bypassed obsidian-daily-notes-interface's own allowPrefixMatch-aware parser. Now routed through getDateFromFile(file, 'week') so weekly notes whose filename only prefix-matches the configured format are revealed too, matching how they're already indexed and dotted.
edge_cases: Does nothing if the active leaf's view isn't a FileView, or the file matches neither day nor week format.

capabilities.name: 1-minute heartbeat keeps 'today' current
capabilities.description: A setInterval every 60s calls tick() (refreshing the `today` moment). If the calendar is currently displaying the current day (`displayedMonth.isSame(today, 'day')`), it also advances `displayedMonth` to the refreshed `today` -- so a calendar left open across midnight rolls over to the new day/month on its own.
behaviour_notes: Cleared onDestroy to avoid leaking the interval when the view closes.
edge_cases: Comparison is `.isSame(today, 'day')` despite the variable name `isViewingCurrentMonth` -- it actually checks same-DAY, not same-month, so browsing to a different day within the current month also disables the auto-rollover until the user navigates back to today.

capabilities.name: Expose the internally-tracked displayed month
capabilities.description: getDisplayedMonth() is a local addition exporting the Svelte component's internal `displayedMonth` binding, so code outside the Svelte tree (view.ts) can read what month the calendar is currently showing.
behaviour_notes: Local fork addition (commit 5ed4307) that exists solely to support month-header-click-open-monthly-note; `displayedMonth` otherwise lives entirely inside obsidian-calendar-ui's component state and wasn't reachable from view.ts before this.

capabilities.name: Resolve a date-UID from a file (day-then-week)
capabilities.description: getDateUIDFromFile() tries to parse the file as a daily note first, then a weekly note, returning obsidian-daily-notes-interface's dateUID string for whichever matches, or null.
behaviour_notes: Backs the activeFile store's setFile().
edge_cases: Own TODO comment: 'I'm not checking the path!' -- a file with a matching basename in an unexpected folder would still resolve, potentially colliding with another note of the same name/date.

capabilities.name: Unicode-aware word count
capabilities.description: getWordCount() tokenizes text with a large Unicode letter-range regex (space-delimited scripts) plus a separate CJK non-space-delimited character class, returning the total token count.
behaviour_notes: Handles CJK text as one 'word' per character (nonSpaceDelimitedWords branch) rather than by whitespace.

capabilities.name: Calendar set data model
capabilities.description: A CalendarSet is a named bundle (id, ctime) holding one optional PeriodicConfig (enabled, format, folder, templatePath, allowPrefixMatch, openAtStartup) per granularity (day/week/month/quarter/year). ISettings.calendarSets is an array of these; ISettings.activeCalendarSet names the one currently in effect.
behaviour_notes: This is the ONLY live config surface in v0.0.17 — see observation about the dead top-level daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/yearly keys.
A calendar set with zero enabled granularities is valid and shown as 'Not configured' in the dashboard card.
edge_cases: Deleting the last remaining calendar set is disabled in the UI (menu item setDisabled when length === 1), but deleteCalendarSet() itself has no such guard if called programmatically.

capabilities.name: Resolve the active calendar set
capabilities.description: getActiveId()/getActiveSet() read settings.activeCalendarSet and find the matching entry in settings.calendarSets.
behaviour_notes: getActiveSet() throws 'No active calendar set found' if activeCalendarSet doesn't match any entry — there is no fallback-to-first-set here (unlike deleteCalendarSet, which does fall back).

capabilities.name: List active/inactive granularities for the active set
capabilities.description: getActiveGranularities() and getInactiveGranularities() filter the fixed granularities[] order array by whether the active set's PeriodicConfig.enabled is true.
behaviour_notes: Order is always day, week, month, quarter, year (granularities[] in types.ts) regardless of insertion order in the calendar set — this fixes ribbon-icon and command ordering.

capabilities.name: Switch the active calendar set
capabilities.description: The 'Switch active calendar set...' command opens a FuzzySuggestModal of all calendar sets; choosing one calls setActiveSet(id), which writes settings.activeCalendarSet and triggers the settings-store subscription.
behaviour_notes: Switching sets re-runs configureCommands()/configureRibbonIcons() and resets the note cache, because onUpdateSettings fires on every settings.subscribe (main.ts:203-210) and cache.reset() listens for the 'periodic-notes:settings-updated' workspace event.

capabilities.name: Create a new calendar set
capabilities.description: createNewCalendarSet(id, refSettings?) pushes a new CalendarSet built from a default per-granularity config, optionally cloning refSettings (used for duplication). Called both by the dashboard's '+' button (empty defaults) and the 'Duplicate calendar set' menu item (existing set as refSettings).
behaviour_notes: Dashboard auto-generates a unique id 'Calendar set N' by probing for the first free suffix; navigates to the new set's Details page with eState.shouldRename=true so the title is immediately editable.
edge_cases: Also used at plugin-load time to synthesize the very first 'Default' calendar set (see legacy-settings-migration).

capabilities.name: Duplicate a calendar set
capabilities.description: The '...' menu on a calendar-set card or Details page's toolbar builds a '<name> copy' id and calls createNewCalendarSet(newId, existingSet), then navigates to it with shouldRename=true.
behaviour_notes: Thin UI wrapper over create-calendar-set with refSettings — kept as its own capability because it is a distinct, user-visible action (menu item), not because the code differs.

capabilities.name: Rename a calendar set inline
capabilities.description: Details.svelte's title is a contenteditable div; on blur, renameCalendarset(oldId, newId) validates uniqueness/non-empty, updates the CalendarSet.id and activeCalendarSet if it was the active one, then the caller navigates the router to the new id.
behaviour_notes: Throws (and the UI catches + refocuses the field) on an empty or duplicate proposed name; a no-op if the name is unchanged.

capabilities.name: Delete a calendar set
capabilities.description: deleteCalendarSet(id) removes the set from settings.calendarSets; if it was the active set, falls back to calendarSets[0].
edge_cases: settings.calendarSets[0] is accessed unconditionally when falling back — deleting the very last calendar set (bypassing the UI's setDisabled guard) would throw on `.id` of undefined.

capabilities.name: Migrate legacy Daily-Notes / pre-calendar-set settings on first load
capabilities.description: On loadSettings(), if calendarSets[] is empty, the plugin checks (in order): (1) does the raw saved data.json look like the pre-calendar-set ILegacySettings shape (top-level daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/yearly keys)? -> migrateLegacySettingsToCalendarSet builds one 'Default' set from all five. (2) does the core Daily Notes internal plugin have non-empty format/folder/template? -> migrateDailyNoteSettings builds a 'Default' set with only 'day' populated. (3) otherwise create a bare 'Default' set with only 'day' enabled.
behaviour_notes: isLegacySettings() is a structural type-guard on the raw loaded object, not on ISettings — it only fires because ISettings itself no longer declares those fields (see the dead-top-level-keys observation).
edge_cases: Path (1) and (2) are mutually exclusive (else-if): a vault with both legacy plugin-data AND live core Daily Notes settings only migrates the plugin-data shape.

capabilities.name: Add/remove per-granularity commands as the active set changes
capabilities.description: configureCommands() removes the 5 commands for every currently-inactive granularity (app.commands.removeCommand) and (re-)adds them for every active one, every time settings change.
behaviour_notes: Command ids are unprefixed inside commands.ts (e.g. 'open-daily-note') but removeCommand needs the fully-qualified `periodic-notes:open-daily-note` — main.ts hardcodes that prefix, which is the manifest.json plugin id, not the vault's dev-install id (see observation on 'periodic-notes-anks').
edge_cases: Runs on every settings change (every keystroke that updates a Writable-bound field, since svelte-writable-derived triggers the parent store), not only when granularities actually toggle — cheap because addCommand/removeCommand are idempotent, but worth knowing for a merge that batches settings writes.

capabilities.name: Ribbon icon for the first active granularity
capabilities.description: configureRibbonIcons() shows exactly one ribbon icon, for the FIRST granularity (in day/week/month/quarter/year order) that is enabled in the active calendar set. Clicking opens/creates today's note for that granularity; meta/cmd-click opens it in a new split; right-click opens a context menu (showFileMenu) listing every active granularity.
behaviour_notes: If no granularity is enabled, no ribbon icon is shown at all.
Local fork commit a8aa7e4 moved this call out of onLayoutReady into onload() directly so ribbon items register before Obsidian applies its ribbon sort order (upstream fix, already on this branch).

capabilities.name: Ribbon right-click menu: open any active granularity's note
capabilities.description: showFileMenu() builds an Obsidian Menu with one item per active granularity ('Open today's daily note', etc.); clicking opens/creates it.

capabilities.name: Create a periodic note
capabilities.description: createPeriodicNote(granularity, date) formats the filename, reads+expands the configured template, resolves/creates the destination folder, and vault.create()s the file. Returns the created TFile.
behaviour_notes: Uses the ACTIVE calendar set's config/format unconditionally — there is no calendarSet parameter, unlike openPeriodicNote which accepts one.
edge_cases: vault.create() throws if a file already exists at the computed path outside the cache's knowledge (e.g. cache not yet initialized) — no existence check is done here.

capabilities.name: Open (or create) a periodic note
capabilities.description: openPeriodicNote(granularity, date, opts?) looks the note up in the cache for the given (or active) calendar set; creates it via createPeriodicNote if missing; opens it in a new split or the current unpinned leaf.
behaviour_notes: This method is explicitly rebound in onload (`this.openPeriodicNote = this.openPeriodicNote.bind(this)`) — a deliberate signal it's meant to be destructured and called by other plugins without losing `this`.

capabilities.name: Look up the exact periodic note for a date
capabilities.description: Cache.getPeriodicNote(calendarSet, granularity, date) linear-scans that calendar set's cache for an EXACT match (matchData.exact === true) whose date isSame(target, granularity); returns the TFile or null. main.ts:getPeriodicNote and the plugin's public getPeriodicNote are thin wrappers.
behaviour_notes: Only ever returns a note whose match was exact — inexact/prefix matches are invisible here even if allowPrefixMatch is on; those surface only via get-periodic-notes-related.

capabilities.name: List all cached notes for a period, optionally including finer granularities
capabilities.description: Cache.getPeriodicNotes(calendarSet, granularity, date, includeFinerGranularities?) returns every cached entry whose date isSame(target, granularity), either restricted to the requested granularity or (with the flag) any granularity at or finer than it (day <= week <= month <= quarter <= year order via compareGranularity). Used by the related-files switcher and the timeline's '+N' badge.
behaviour_notes: main.ts:getPeriodicNotes (the plugin's public wrapper) carries the author's own '// TODO: What API do I want for this?' comment — treat the includeFinerGranularities boolean-flag shape as unsettled.

capabilities.name: Check whether a file path is a periodic note
capabilities.description: Cache.isPeriodic(path, granularity?) scans every calendar set's cache for an entry at that path, optionally filtered to one granularity. Used by every command's checkCallback to decide whether jump/open-adjacent should be enabled.

capabilities.name: Find the next/previous periodic note of the same granularity
capabilities.description: Cache.findAdjacent(calendarSet, filePath, direction) sorts that calendar set's same-granularity entries by canonicalDateStr (an ISO string) and returns the neighbour one position forwards or backwards.
behaviour_notes: Re-sorts the ENTIRE calendar-set/granularity slice on every call rather than maintaining a sorted structure — fine at personal-vault scale, a hazard if the merged plugin targets much larger vaults.
edge_cases: Includes inexact/prefix matches in the sort, so 'adjacent' can land on a loosely-matched note, not just an exact one.

capabilities.name: Jump to the closest existing adjacent note (no creation)
capabilities.description: 'Jump forwards/backwards to closest <periodicity> note': looks up the active file's cache metadata, calls find-adjacent-note, opens the result if found or shows a Notice ('There's no ... note before/after this') if not.
behaviour_notes: Never creates a note — pure navigation, distinct from open-adjacent-note-command.

capabilities.name: Open the next/previous note by date offset (creating it if needed)
capabilities.description: 'Open next/previous <periodicity> note': computes the active file's date +/- 1 unit of its own granularity and calls openPeriodicNote, creating the note if it doesn't exist yet.
behaviour_notes: Unlike jump-to-adjacent-note-command, this always succeeds (by creating), which is why an older commit (b517af8, 'jump backwards will create new notes') exists upstream distinguishing the two behaviors.

capabilities.name: Find a file's cache metadata (any or a specific calendar set)
capabilities.description: Cache.find(filePath, calendarSet?) looks the path up directly if a calendar set is given; otherwise checks the active set first, then every other set. Wrapped by main.ts's findInCache.

capabilities.name: Auto-open a configured note on vault load
capabilities.description: On workspace.onLayoutReady, findStartupNoteConfig() scans every calendar set/granularity for openAtStartup===true and, if found, calls openPeriodicNote for today's date in that calendar set.
behaviour_notes: Only the FIRST match found (iterating calendarSets then granularities in fixed order) is opened, which is consistent with clear-startup-note-exclusivity enforcing at most one such flag vault-wide.

capabilities.name: Enforce a single startup-note flag vault-wide
capabilities.description: clearStartupNote() walks every calendar set and granularity, clearing openAtStartup wherever it's true. Called by OpenAtStartupSetting.svelte just before setting the newly-toggled one, so turning on one 'Open at startup' switch turns off every other one, across all calendar sets.
behaviour_notes: This is a quiet, easy-to-lose-in-a-merge invariant: the setting's own type (PeriodicConfig.openAtStartup: boolean) does not enforce exclusivity; it's enforced only by this call-site convention.
edge_cases: Only invoked from the toggle's onChange when turning it ON — toggling one OFF does not re-run it (no-op needed anyway).

capabilities.name: Template token expansion
capabilities.description: applyTemplateTransformations(filename, granularity, date, format, templateContents) replaces {{date}}/{{time}}/{{title}} always, plus granularity-specific tokens: day gets {{yesterday}}, {{tomorrow}}, and {{date|time (+/-N unit)(:format)}}; week gets {{sunday:fmt}}..{{saturday:fmt}} (day-of-week relative to the note's week); month/quarter/year get {{month|quarter|year (+/-N unit)(:format)}} anchored to startOf(that unit).
behaviour_notes: The +/-N calc tokens borrow the CURRENT wall-clock hour/minute/second (via window.moment() 'now'), not the target date's own time-of-day, before adding the offset.
Also reused for RE-templating on template-file changes via applyPeriodicTemplateToFile (utils.ts:228-247), not just at creation time.
edge_cases: Regexes are case-insensitive and tolerate arbitrary whitespace inside {{ }}, but a malformed calc suffix (e.g. missing unit letter) simply fails to match and passes the token through unexpanded.

capabilities.name: Resolve creation path and auto-create missing folders
capabilities.description: getNoteCreationPath(app, filename, config) joins config.folder + filename (+.md), normalizes it, and ensureFolderExists() creates every missing intermediate folder via vault.createFolder before returning the path.
behaviour_notes: join()/basename() are a small hand-rolled path.js (credited to @creationix/path.js in a comment) rather than using Obsidian's normalizePath alone — handles multi-segment folder+filename joining with '.' segment stripping.
edge_cases: ensureFolderExists checks only the immediate parent folder existence in one shot (vault.createFolder can itself create intermediate segments in Obsidian's API), not each ancestor individually.

capabilities.name: Strict-then-prefix date parsing (getDateWithPrefixFallback)
capabilities.description: For each candidate format (strictest first): try window.moment(input, format, true) (strict mode) and return isExactMatch:true on the first success. If none succeed strictly, retry every format in NON-strict mode; accept the first result where date.format(format) is a PREFIX of the original input string (isExactMatch:false). Returns {date: null, isExactMatch: false} if nothing matches either way.
behaviour_notes: Local fork addition, commit e50b8e8. The canonical example from the commit message: filename '2026-W07, 09.02 - 15.02.md' does not strictly match format 'gggg-[W]ww', but a loose parse reformats to '2026-W07' which IS a prefix of the filename, so it's accepted as an inexact match.

The prefix check is a plain string startsWith on the REFORMATTED date, not a regex against the original format — so it only works when the format's literal/moment output naturally forms a prefix of real filenames (works well for '<date>, <suffix>' naming, not for '<suffix> <date>' naming).
edge_cases: Whether the inexact-match branch is even allowed to win depends on the caller passing allowPrefixMatch=true (cache.ts gates it, not this function itself — this function always computes and returns the fallback result regardless of the setting).

capabilities.name: Possible-formats expansion for nested-path formats
capabilities.description: getPossibleFormats(calendarSet, granularity) returns [fullFormat] normally, or [fullFormat, basenameOnlyFormat] when the configured format contains a '/' (e.g. 'YYYY/YYYY-MM-DD'), so matching can succeed whether or not the note was later moved out of its dated subfolder.

capabilities.name: Vault-wide loose date guess when no configured format matches at all
capabilities.description: getLooselyMatchedDate(basename) tries, in order, a full YYYY-MM-DD-ish regex, then a YYYY-MM-ish regex, then a bare 4-digit-year regex, returning the first hit as {date, granularity}. Used by cache.resolve() as a last resort per calendar set when no active granularity's folder+format matched the file.
behaviour_notes: A week regex (WEEK_PREFIX) is written but commented out with a TODO about ISO-week ambiguity — week granularity is never guessed loosely.
edge_cases: See observation: this fallback is NOT folder-scoped in the caller (cache.resolve()), so it can match files anywhere in the vault, not just under the calendar set's configured folders.

capabilities.name: Warn when a nested-path format's basename can't uniquely identify a day
capabilities.description: validateFormatComplexity(format, granularity) returns 'loose-parsing' if the format doesn't round-trip through a strict parse at all, or 'fragile-basename' if (for day granularity, with a '/' in the format) the basename portion is missing a day/month/year token letter — surfaced as an inline warning with a frontmatter workaround suggestion in NoteFormatSetting.svelte.
behaviour_notes: getDateInput() (settings/validation.ts:84-98) is the consumer of this classification in the cache path: when fragile-basename, it reconstructs a multi-segment 'path suffix' string (matching the format's nesting depth) instead of just file.basename before handing it to date parsing.

capabilities.name: Validate a format string
capabilities.description: validateFormat(format, granularity) rejects illegal filename characters/control chars/reserved Windows names, and (for day granularity only) checks that formatting 'now' and re-parsing strictly round-trips.
behaviour_notes: The strict round-trip check only runs for granularity === 'day' — week/month/quarter/year formats are only checked for illegal characters, not parseability, at input time (parseability issues there surface later via validateFormatComplexity's 'loose-parsing' warning instead).

capabilities.name: Validate a folder path
capabilities.description: validateFolder(app, folder) accepts empty or '/' as valid (vault root); otherwise checks the normalized path exists in the vault.
behaviour_notes: Only validates existence, not creatability — actual folder creation happens lazily at note-creation time (ensureFolderExists), so a not-yet-existing folder is a UI warning, not a hard block.

capabilities.name: Validate a template file path
capabilities.description: validateTemplate(app, template) resolves the path via metadataCache.getFirstLinkpathDest and reports 'Template file not found' if it doesn't resolve.

capabilities.name: Build the full note-cache index on vault layout-ready
capabilities.description: PeriodicNotesCache.initialize() walks, for every calendar set and every active granularity's configured folder, the folder's file tree (memoized recursion) and runs resolve()+resolveChangedMetadata() on each file, populating cachedFiles: Map<calendarSetId, Map<filePath, metadata>>.
behaviour_notes: Runs once at workspace.onLayoutReady, not at plugin onload — avoids racing Obsidian's own initial vault/metadata indexing.
edge_cases: A folder path that doesn't exist yet (getAbstractFileByPath returns null/undefined) is silently skipped by the memoized recursor's `if (!rootFolder) return` guard.

capabilities.name: Resolve a single file against every calendar set on create
capabilities.description: resolve(file, reason) checks each calendar set (skipping if a frontmatter match already exists for that path), then each active granularity: folder-prefix match, then strict-then-prefix date parsing gated by allowPrefixMatch, then (if nothing matched for any granularity in that set) the vault-wide loose fallback. On a match it caches the metadata, fires 'periodic-notes:resolve', and — if this is a brand-new EMPTY file — auto-applies the granularity's template.
behaviour_notes: Registered on vault 'create' — fires for every new file in the vault, not just ones under a configured folder; the folder-prefix check (`file.path.startsWith(folder)`) is the actual filter.
edge_cases: 'frontmatter supersedes filename': if a path already has a frontmatter-sourced cache entry for this calendar set, the filename-matching branch is skipped entirely for that set (continue calendarsets) — but a NEW filename match can still overwrite an existing filename-sourced entry.

capabilities.name: Re-resolve a file on rename
capabilities.description: resolveRename(file, oldPath) deletes the old path from every calendar-set cache and re-runs resolve() on the new path.
behaviour_notes: Iterates ALL calendar-set caches to delete oldPath (not just the one(s) it was cached under) — harmless but O(n) over calendar sets per rename.

capabilities.name: Resolve a file via a frontmatter date field
capabilities.description: resolveChangedMetadata(file, _, cache) is registered on metadataCache 'changed'. For each calendar set/active granularity whose folder prefixes the file path, if the frontmatter has a string entry keyed by the granularity name (e.g. `day: 2022-02-02`), it's parsed STRICTLY against DEFAULT_FORMAT[granularity] (not the calendar set's configured format) and cached as an exact, matchType:'frontmatter' entry.
behaviour_notes: This is the path referenced by NoteFormatSetting.svelte's warning text ('include `<granularity>: <DEFAULT_FORMAT>` in your template frontmatter') for loose-parsing/fragile-basename formats.
edge_cases: Ignores the calendar set's own configured format and its allowPrefixMatch flag entirely — see observation on the asymmetry with the filename-based resolve() path.

capabilities.name: Rebuild the cache whenever settings change
capabilities.description: The cache listens for the 'periodic-notes:settings-updated' workspace event (fired on every settings.subscribe callback, i.e. every save) and calls reset(), which clears cachedFiles and re-runs initialize().
behaviour_notes: A full vault-tree rescan on every settings save (including a single keystroke in a format field, since PeriodicGroup's writable-derived store writes through to the parent settings store on each bound input) — a performance hazard on large vaults that a merge should consider debouncing.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity opt-in gate for prefix-matched notes
capabilities.description: In cache.resolve(), a filename's inexact/prefix match (isExactMatch===false from getDateWithPrefixFallback) is only accepted into the cache if that granularity's PeriodicConfig.allowPrefixMatch is true; an exact match is always accepted regardless.
behaviour_notes: Local fork addition, commit e50b8e8, default false — off by default so existing vaults don't suddenly start absorbing loosely-named files.

capabilities.name: Auto-apply the template to a manually-created empty file that matches a periodic pattern
capabilities.description: When resolve() is triggered by vault 'create' (not 'initialize') and the newly created file is empty (file.stat.size === 0), applyPeriodicTemplateToFile() renders and writes the granularity's template into it — so creating an empty file by hand with the right name (e.g. via 'New note') gets templated exactly as if openPeriodicNote had created it.
behaviour_notes: A quiet behavior easy to lose in a merge: this is the ONLY path that templates a file NOT created through createPeriodicNote/openPeriodicNote.
edge_cases: Does not fire during initialize() (reason !== 'create'), so pre-existing empty files at startup are never auto-templated, only ones created while the plugin is running.

capabilities.name: Override the global moment.js week-start day
capabilities.description: overrideGlobalMomentWeekStart(weekStart) saves the bundled locale's original week-spec once (window._bundledLocaleWeekSpec), then calls moment.updateLocale to either restore it ('locale') or force a specific day-of-week as dow.
behaviour_notes: This mutates the GLOBAL moment.js locale object shared by the whole Obsidian process — it affects every other plugin's date formatting too, and the settings UI says so explicitly ('may impact other plugins as well').

capabilities.name: One-time global moment.js locale configuration at plugin load
capabilities.description: configureGlobalMomentLocale(localeOverride, weekStart) maps Obsidian's UI language (or the user's explicit override, or a more-specific system locale) to a moment.js locale string and calls moment.locale(); initializeLocaleConfigOnce guards this to run only once per session via window._hasConfiguredLocale, regardless of how many times the plugin reloads.
behaviour_notes: The window._hasConfiguredLocale guard means DISABLING and RE-ENABLING the plugin within the same Obsidian session will not re-apply a changed localeOverride until a full reload — a subtle staleness trap.

capabilities.name: Human-readable relative date/period labels
capabilities.description: getRelativeDate(granularity, date): for 'week', special-cases this/last/next week then falls back to moment.duration(...).humanize(true); for 'day', uses moment's calendar() with custom lastWeek/lastDay/sameDay/nextDay/nextWeek/sameElse formatters; for month/quarter/year, plain date.format(HUMANIZE_FORMAT[granularity]).

capabilities.name: Settings mini-app breadcrumb router
capabilities.description: The `router` writable store holds a breadcrumb path (['Periodic Notes'] or ['Periodic Notes', <calendarSetId>]) plus an eState bag; navigate()/reset() drive which page Router.svelte renders and can carry one-shot flags (e.g. shouldRename) read by the destination page's onMount.
behaviour_notes: reset() is called from Router.svelte's onDestroy, i.e. whenever the settings tab is closed — so reopening settings always starts back at the dashboard, never resumes on the last-viewed calendar set.

capabilities.name: Settings dashboard: list, add calendar sets, global toggles
capabilities.description: Dashboard.svelte shows the getting-started banner (if not dismissed), a grid of calendar-set cards with a '+' to add one, the 'enable timeline complication' toggle, and the vault-wide week-start/locale dropdowns.

capabilities.name: Settings details page: rename, activate/duplicate/delete, per-granularity accordion
capabilities.description: Details.svelte for one calendar set: inline-editable title (rename), an 'Active' badge, an options menu (set active / duplicate / delete, delete disabled if it's the only set), and one PeriodicGroup accordion row per granularity.
behaviour_notes: Contains the local fork's scroll-guard crash fix (see observation) at onMount.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity Format setting
capabilities.description: NoteFormatSetting.svelte: text input bound to calendarSets[].<g>.format; shows a live moment.js preview and validation error/complexity warning.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity Note Folder setting
capabilities.description: NoteFolderSetting.svelte: text input with FolderSuggest autocomplete, bound to calendarSets[].<g>.folder, validated on blur.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity Note Template setting
capabilities.description: NoteTemplateSetting.svelte: text input with FileSuggest autocomplete, bound to calendarSets[].<g>.templatePath, validated on blur.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity Open on startup toggle
capabilities.description: OpenAtStartupSetting.svelte: toggle bound to calendarSets[].<g>.openAtStartup; turning it on first calls clearStartupNote across the whole settings tree.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity Allow prefix matching toggle
capabilities.description: AllowPrefixMatchSetting.svelte: toggle bound to calendarSets[].<g>.allowPrefixMatch, with an inline example in its description.
behaviour_notes: Local fork addition (commit e50b8e8), modeled directly on OpenAtStartupSetting.svelte's structure; no upstream equivalent.

capabilities.name: Detect and offer to migrate away from the core Daily Notes plugin
capabilities.description: GettingStartedBanner.svelte checks isDailyNotesPluginEnabled()/hasLegacyDailyNoteSettings() and, if the core plugin is enabled, offers a 'Disable' button (disableDailyNotesPlugin) with a reminder to update hotkeys.

capabilities.name: Natural-language date switcher
capabilities.description: 'Show date switcher...' opens NLDNavigator, a SuggestModal that (a) tries a small set of hand-written regex shortcuts (next/last/this <weekday|week|month|year>, 'in N units'/'N units ago', and bare today/yesterday/tomorrow/this-last-next week/month/year), filtered to active granularities and startsWith-matched against the query; (b) otherwise defers to the nldates-obsidian plugin's parseDate() for free-text parsing, then infers a granularity from the query text (week/month/quarter/year keyword, else day).
behaviour_notes: Only registered as a command when app.plugins.getPlugin('nldates-obsidian') exists (checked in checkCallback) — this whole capability is inert without that third-party plugin installed.

Cmd/Ctrl+Enter opens the selected item without closing the modal chooser's own key handling — implemented by reaching into the private, unexposed `this.chooser` via an `any` cast (obsidian.d.ts doesn't type it), a fragile dependency on Obsidian's internal SuggestModal implementation.
edge_cases: Quarter suggestions are commented out throughout ('TODO include once nldates supports quarters') — quarter notes are reachable only via the calendar sets UI/commands, not via this switcher's quick suggestions.

capabilities.name: Related-files switcher with modal hand-off
capabilities.description: Pressing Tab inside NLDNavigator closes it and opens RelatedFilesSwitcher scoped to the currently-selected date/granularity, listing every inexact-matched note for that period (optionally including finer granularities via Shift+8). Pressing Tab again closes it and reopens NLDNavigator, replaying the original query text via a synthetic 'input' event.
behaviour_notes: This chain (close-modal-A, open-modal-B, replay-query-via-synthetic-event) is stateful UI glue with no test coverage visible in the repo — a straightforward place to silently break during a merge if either modal's constructor signature or the 'Tab' scope registration changes.

capabilities.name: Quick-switch active calendar set via fuzzy modal
capabilities.description: CalendarSetSuggestModal (a FuzzySuggestModal) lists all calendar sets by id; selecting one calls setActiveSet.
behaviour_notes: getItemText() calls `item.toString()` on a CalendarSet object (relying on default Object toString / '[object Object]' fallback quirks are avoided only because Obsidian's FuzzySuggestModal actually calls getItemText for both matching AND fallback rendering) — this looks like it should be `item.id`; works today only because renderSuggestion overrides the visible text.

capabilities.name: Generic popper-positioned text-input autocomplete
capabilities.description: TextInputSuggest (abstract base) plus FileSuggest/FolderSuggest: wires an input's focus/input/blur events to a Suggest dropdown positioned via @popperjs/core, with arrow-key navigation and a shared Obsidian Scope pushed/popped on open/close.
behaviour_notes: FileSuggest/FolderSuggest do no fuzzy ranking — plain case-insensitive substring `contains()` filtering, unbounded (renders every match, no result cap), which could get slow in very large vaults.

capabilities.name: Timeline complication badge and week strip
capabilities.description: Timeline.svelte renders a small badge (relative date label, e.g. 'Today'/'Last week', plus a forward-arrow icon if the note was only inexactly matched) fixed top-right of any open periodic note; clicking expands a 7-day strip (starting the note's locale week) with the note's own day highlighted and today marked; clicking a day opens/creates that day's note. Controlled by the enableTimelineComplication setting and re-checked on file-open and cache-resolve events.
edge_cases: Nothing renders at all if the current view's file isn't found in the cache (cache.find returns null) — periodicData stays null and the {#if} guard hides the whole complication.

capabilities.name: Mount/unmount one Timeline component per open markdown leaf
capabilities.description: TimelineManager listens for workspace 'layout-change', diffs the set of open MarkdownView containerEls against its own tracked Svelte component instances, destroys ones whose leaf closed, and mounts a new Timeline into any view that doesn't have one yet.
behaviour_notes: cleanup() (called from plugin.unload) destroys every tracked component but does NOT unregister the 'layout-change' listener itself directly — that's handled by Obsidian's registerEvent auto-cleanup on plugin unload, not by this class.
edge_cases: Matching a Svelte component to its leaf is done by comparing `$$.root` (an internal Svelte instance field) to the view's containerEl — relies on undocumented Svelte internals rather than a public API.

capabilities.name: Open the calendar view
capabilities.description: Registers the 'Show calendar' command; reveals (or creates in the right sidebar) the single calendaric-calendar leaf.
behaviour_notes: Only one calendar leaf is ever created (checks getLeavesOfType before creating another).
No ribbon icon is registered anywhere — command palette is the only entry point, despite CalendarView.getIcon() defining a 'calendar' icon.

capabilities.name: Render the month grid
capabilities.description: Builds a 6x7 HTML table for the displayed month: weekday headers respecting week-start, optional week-number column, today/adjacent-month/weekend styling per cell.
behaviour_notes: Always renders exactly 6 weeks regardless of month length — covered by src/ui/calendarUtils.test.ts ('returns 6 weeks for any month').
Adjacent-month / weekend / week-number flags all covered by src/ui/calendarUtils.test.ts.
The widget itself (calendar.ts render/renderGrid DOM assembly) has zero test coverage.
edge_cases: Leap-year Feb 29 handling verified by test.
Dec-to-Jan year boundary handled (adjacent Jan days get year()+1) — verified by test.

capabilities.name: Resolve the calendar's week-start day
capabilities.description: Converts the 'weekStart' setting ('locale' or a named weekday) to a numeric 0-6 weekday used only for grid layout (which column Monday..Sunday lands in, and where the grid starts).
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/ui/calendarUtils.test.ts for 'monday', 'sunday', and 'locale'.
edge_cases: This setting affects ONLY grid layout. It does NOT affect week-token resolution (see observation on week-token-in-format-field) — the two 'week start' concepts are inconsistent within the plugin.

capabilities.name: Navigate the calendar (prev/next/today)
capabilities.description: Nav buttons move the displayed month back/forward one month or jump to the current month; only the grid body + title re-render (not the whole widget).
behaviour_notes: No test coverage — DOM/event-driven, not exercised by vitest.

capabilities.name: Show a dot under days/weeks with an existing note
capabilities.description: Scans the vault (by recomputing every note path for the visible month/weeks and checking vault.getAbstractFileByPath) to decide which day cells and the week-number cell get a small SVG dot.
behaviour_notes: No cache: re-derives the full set of expected paths every render. No test coverage.
Returns an empty set immediately when the granularity's config.enabled or config.format is falsy — so disabling day/week notes silently removes their dots too.
edge_cases: Week dots are keyed by the ISO Monday of each visible week, independent of the weekStart display setting.

capabilities.name: Live-update dots on vault changes
capabilities.description: DotScanner registers vault 'create', 'delete', and 'rename' listeners; any of them triggers a full grid re-render so dots stay in sync without the user reloading the view.
behaviour_notes: Listeners are properly unregistered in destroy() via app.vault.offref — no test coverage but the cleanup pattern matches AGENTS.md's register*/cleanup guidance.

capabilities.name: Highlight the currently open note in the grid
capabilities.description: Listens to workspace 'file-open' and adds an 'is-active' class to the day/week cell whose computed path matches the newly opened file.
behaviour_notes: Recomputes the path for every day/week cell on every file-open event, no memoization. No test coverage.

capabilities.name: Auto-refresh the grid every 60s
capabilities.description: CalendarView registers a 60-second interval that calls calendar.refresh() so the 'today' cell rolls over at midnight without requiring user interaction.
behaviour_notes: Uses this.registerInterval so it is cleaned up on view close, per AGENTS.md guidance. No test coverage.

capabilities.name: Click a day/week cell to open or create its note
capabilities.description: Clicking a cell for an enabled granularity looks up the note; if it exists, opens it (openNote, respecting meta/ctrl for split); if not, either creates it directly or shows a confirmation modal first, per the confirmBeforeCreate setting.
behaviour_notes: Cells for a disabled granularity are not clickable at all (cursor/click handler only attached when config.enabled). No test coverage — this is the main uncovered interaction path.

capabilities.name: Confirmation modal before creating a note
capabilities.description: Generic accept/dismiss modal ('New <Granularity> Note' / 'File X does not exist. Would you like to create it?'); onAccept runs the actual create+open.
behaviour_notes: Explicitly commented as 'Copied from calendar-plugin's ConfirmationModal structure' — i.e. already a manual, non-Svelte port of that source's modal. No test coverage.

capabilities.name: Create a periodic note (day or week only)
capabilities.description: Computes the note path, creates parent folders if missing, reads+substitutes the configured template if any, and calls vault.create(). Returns the created TFile.
behaviour_notes: Type-level restriction: createNote's granularity parameter is typed as "day" | "week" only — month/quarter/year are not representable, not just unimplemented.
No test coverage for noteCreate.ts (it touches app.vault.create, which needs a fuller Obsidian mock than exists today).
edge_cases: Does not open the file — caller's responsibility (documented in the file's own comment).

capabilities.name: Apply a template file when creating a note
capabilities.description: If config.templatePath resolves to a file (via metadataCache.getFirstLinkpathDest), its content is read and passed through substituteTemplateTokens before being written as the new note's content; otherwise the note is created empty.
behaviour_notes: No test coverage (requires app.vault.read + metadataCache mocking).
edge_cases: Silently returns empty string if templatePath is set but does not resolve to a real file.

capabilities.name: Open a note, reuse tab or split on meta/ctrl-click
capabilities.description: Opens a TFile via workspace.getLeaf(false) (reuse an unpinned tab) normally, or workspace.getLeaf("split") when the click carries metaKey/ctrlKey.
behaviour_notes: No test coverage.

capabilities.name: Open a note in a new tab (startup path)
capabilities.description: Opens a TFile via workspace.getLeaf("tab"); used exclusively by the startup-note flow, not by grid clicks.
behaviour_notes: No test coverage.

capabilities.name: Compute a periodic note's vault path
capabilities.description: Combines a resolved folder with a Format-string filename (moment.js tokens plus Calendaric's {{weekday:fmt}} week tokens) to produce the full '<folder>/<filename>.md' path for a given date and PeriodicConfig.
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/notes/noteUtils.test.ts: folder present/absent, week-token format, and the Obsidian-default-folder fallback.

capabilities.name: Fall back to Obsidian's default new-file folder
capabilities.description: When a granularity's own 'folder' setting is empty, reads the vault's internal config (newFileLocation / newFileFolderPath) to decide where the note goes: the configured folder if newFileLocation === 'folder', otherwise the vault root.
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/notes/noteUtils.test.ts ('uses Obsidian default folder when config folder is empty and newFileLocation=folder').
edge_cases: Reads app.vault.config via an untyped 'as any' cast — this is Obsidian's undocumented internal vault config, not public API.

capabilities.name: Week token in the Format field: {{weekday:fmt}}
capabilities.description: In a Weekly Note's Format string only, {{monday:fmt}}..{{sunday:fmt}} is replaced with that ISO weekday's date (relative to the note's own date) formatted with the given moment.js format, then the whole string is escaped as a moment.js literal before being run through date.format(). Documented in docs/guide.md under 'Format Field > Week tokens'.
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/notes/noteUtils.test.ts and src/notes/templateTokens.test.ts (multiple cases: single token, full range format, case-insensitivity, no-op on plain strings).
edge_cases: Weekday resolution is always ISO (Monday=1..Sunday=7), REGARDLESS of the weekStart setting. docs/guide.md line 37 claims tokens 'are resolved using the same week-start locale as your Start week on setting' — that claim does not match the code (see observations).
Weekday matching is case-insensitive ('Monday', 'MONDAY' both work).

capabilities.name: Week token in template body: {{weekday:fmt}}
capabilities.description: Same {{monday:fmt}}..{{sunday:fmt}} tokens, evaluated a second time against the note's body text (not the filename) — only for granularity 'week'.
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/notes/templateTokens.test.ts ('substitutes full weekly template', 'does not substitute {{monday:fmt}} for daily granularity').

capabilities.name: {{date}} template variable
capabilities.description: Replaced with the note's own date, formatted with the granularity's configured Format string (week tokens included).
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/notes/templateTokens.test.ts.

capabilities.name: {{date:fmt}} template variable
capabilities.description: Replaced with the note's date using a caller-supplied moment.js format string, distinct from the note's configured Format.
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/notes/templateTokens.test.ts. Note: substitution order matters — {{date:fmt}} is replaced before {{date}} specifically to avoid the plain {{date}} regex matching inside it; test 'does not substitute {{date:custom}} as {{date}}' asserts this.

capabilities.name: {{time}} template variable
capabilities.description: Replaced with the current time as HH:mm (the moment passed into substituteTemplateTokens, i.e. creation time).
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/notes/templateTokens.test.ts.

capabilities.name: {{title}} template variable
capabilities.description: Replaced with the created note's filename (without .md extension).
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/notes/templateTokens.test.ts.

capabilities.name: {{yesterday}} / {{tomorrow}} template variables
capabilities.description: Daily-note-only: replaced with the previous/next calendar day, formatted with the daily granularity's configured Format string.
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/notes/templateTokens.test.ts, including that it's a no-op ('left untouched') for granularity 'week'.

capabilities.name: Open a periodic note automatically on vault startup
capabilities.description: On workspace.onLayoutReady, checks each granularity in order (day, week, month, quarter, year) for the first with openAtStartup+enabled; opens the existing file, or silently creates it (bypassing confirmBeforeCreate) if missing — but only for day/week.
behaviour_notes: No test coverage.
edge_cases: If a month/quarter/year granularity somehow has openAtStartup=true and no existing file, the loop 'break's without opening anything for that key and does not fall through to try the next granularity — effectively a silent no-op, not a crash.

In practice month/quarter/year can never reach openAtStartup=true today: the settings UI's placeholder groups for those granularities render a permanently-disabled toggle and no per-granularity content section at all (see calendaric-settings).

capabilities.name: Enforce only one granularity can auto-open at startup
capabilities.description: clearStartupNote(settings) sets openAtStartup=false on all five granularities; called by the settings UI right before setting the new one's openAtStartup=true.
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/settings.test.ts (clears all granularities; no-op when already false; leaves other fields untouched).

capabilities.name: Import settings from the core Daily Notes plugin
capabilities.description: When the core 'daily-notes' internal plugin is enabled, shows a callout in the settings tab offering to copy its format/folder/template into Calendaric's day config (marking day.enabled=true and hasMigratedDailyNoteSettings=true), disable the core plugin outright, or dismiss the callout.
behaviour_notes: No test coverage for renderImportCard itself (DOM-heavy); the functions it calls (isDailyNotesPluginEnabled, getLegacyDailyNoteSettings, disableDailyNotesPlugin) are fully covered by src/settings/dailyNotesImport.test.ts.
edge_cases: If legacy format is empty, falls back to the hardcoded default 'YYYY-MM-DD' rather than leaving it blank.
There is no equivalent import path for the Periodic Notes plugin's week/month/quarter/year settings — only Daily Notes import exists.

capabilities.name: Read the core Daily Notes plugin's config
capabilities.description: Reads app.internalPlugins.getPluginById('daily-notes').instance.options (format/folder/template) via an untyped internal-API cast; also exposes isDailyNotesPluginEnabled().
behaviour_notes: Fully covered by src/settings/dailyNotesImport.test.ts: enabled/disabled/not-found/missing-internalPlugins, and every combination of present/missing format/folder/template.
edge_cases: Missing any individual option field defaults that field to an empty string rather than throwing.

capabilities.name: Disable the core Daily Notes plugin
capabilities.description: Calls the internal Daily Notes plugin's disable(true) to turn it off from within Calendaric's settings tab.
behaviour_notes: Covered by src/settings/dailyNotesImport.test.ts ('calls disable(true) on the plugin', 'does not throw when the plugin is not found').

capabilities.name: Open the bundled format/template guide from settings
capabilities.description: A 'Format & template guide' link in the Format field's description opens docs/guide.md (the plugin's own bundled doc) using Electron's shell.openPath, built from the vault adapter's basePath plus a hardcoded plugin-id path.
behaviour_notes: No test coverage.
edge_cases: Uses (window as any).require('electron') — an Electron/desktop-only API. manifest.json declares isDesktopOnly: false, so this link will throw on mobile where window.require does not exist (see observations).

capabilities.name: Override the moment.js locale
capabilities.description: A dropdown of all moment.js-registered locales; changing it calls window.moment.locale(value) immediately (affecting all date formatting app-wide for this session) and persists the choice. Applied again on every plugin onload if set.
behaviour_notes: No test coverage.
edge_cases: Calling window.moment.locale() is global/process-wide — it changes locale for every other plugin using the shared moment instance too, not just Calendaric.

capabilities.name: Non-functional Monthly/Quarterly/Yearly/Custom Notes settings groups
capabilities.description: The Periodic Notes settings section renders a heading row with a permanently-disabled toggle for 'Monthly Notes', 'Quarterly Notes', 'Yearly Notes', and 'Custom Notes', with no expandable content and no way to enable them from the UI.
behaviour_notes: No test coverage.
edge_cases: 'Custom Notes' has no backing PeriodicConfig or granularity key anywhere in types.ts/settings.ts at all — it's UI scaffolding for a feature that doesn't exist yet even as a data shape.

capabilities.name: Daily note folder/format/template is defined in three places at once
capabilities.description: The same daily-note folder ('_00 Planer/_01 Dziennik'), filename format ('YYYY-MM-DD, dddd') and template path are configured independently in periodic-notes-anks.calendarSets[0].day, the core daily-notes.json, and templater's folder_templates entry for that folder. All three currently agree, but nothing keeps them in sync.
behaviour_notes: core daily-notes.json template path has no .md extension ('Daily Template') while the others do; Obsidian's TFile resolution tolerates this, but a naive string-compare in a merged plugin would not.
edge_cases: If any one of the three configs is edited without the others, whichever plugin actually creates the file wins silently.

capabilities.name: Create a daily note
capabilities.description: A new file matching the daily folder/format is created (by periodic-notes-anks's calendar UI, the core Daily Notes command, or manually), and because trigger_on_file_creation_mode is 'folder', Templater auto-runs Daily Template.md against it.
behaviour_notes: Actual file creation is done by an external plugin (periodic-notes-anks or core daily-notes), out of scope of this vault's own code; Templater only reacts to the folder.

capabilities.name: Daily note frontmatter (month/week links + tags)
capabilities.description: Parses the date from the file title (must start with YYYY-MM-DD), then writes frontmatter linking both the personal and Work monthly notes and the weekly note, plus journal/journal-daily tags.
behaviour_notes: Aborts with a visible warning block instead of throwing if the title doesn't start with YYYY-MM-DD or moment can't parse it (Daily Template.md:20-30).
edge_cases: Title must literally start with YYYY-MM-DD; a note renamed or created with a different prefix silently gets the warning block as its entire content.

capabilities.name: Anchored backlink from daily note to today's Work-monthly heading
capabilities.description: Computes the current month's Work note title, reads that file's raw content, and only emits a `[[Month - Work#DD.MM, dddd]]` link under '# Today' if the matching '## DD.MM, dddd' heading is actually found via regex in that file's body.
behaviour_notes: Silently omits the link (no warning) if the Work-monthly note doesn't exist yet or the heading isn't found — e.g. weekend days, since headers are only generated Mon-Fri (isoWeekday() <= 5).
edge_cases: Depends on exact heading text match; renaming/reformatting a heading in the Work-monthly note breaks the link silently for that day only.

capabilities.name: Auto-create this week's weekly note from the daily template
capabilities.description: After computing the current week's pretty title, checks whether that exact file already exists at '_00 Planer/_02 Tygodnie/<pretty title>.md'; if not, calls tp.file.create_new on the Weekly Periodic Template to create it (open_new=false, so focus stays on the daily note being edited).
behaviour_notes: Checks only the pretty path, relying on the invariant that Weekly Periodic Template always renames/moves itself into that exact pretty form (Daily Template.md:73-75 comment).
If the weekly template file itself can't be found by tp.file.find_tfile, emits a warning instead of failing (Daily Template.md:82-84).
edge_cases: If a weekly note was ever created under a different name/location (e.g. templater misfire), this check won't see it and will create a duplicate.

capabilities.name: Rename raw weekly title to pretty, move into target folder
capabilities.description: Extracts the ISO week (YYYY-Wnn) from either a raw or already-pretty file title, computes the pretty title 'GGGG-[W]WW, DD.MM - DD.MM', renames the file to it, and moves it into '_00 Planer/_02 Tygodnie' if not already there.
behaviour_notes: Uses tp.config.target_file rather than app.workspace.getActiveFile() specifically because this template can run on a file that isn't the active/open note (created programmatically by the daily template) — documented in-file at lines 66-71.
ensureFolder() creates parent folders recursively since Obsidian's createFolder requires parents to pre-exist (lines 17-27).
edge_cases: Week parsing regex only matches a leading '\d{4}-W\d{2}'; a title not starting that way aborts with a warning (lines 32-36).

capabilities.name: Weekly note frontmatter (month/year links) + prev/next navigation
capabilities.description: From the Monday of the ISO week, computes and writes month (personal + Work) and year (personal + 1on1 Self Review) frontmatter links, journal/journal-weekly tags, and a prev/next line linking the adjacent pretty weekly titles.

capabilities.name: Weekly note's inline daily-note listing (dataviewjs)
capabilities.description: A dataviewjs block parses the weekly note's own filename ('YYYY-Www, DD.MM - DD.MM') into a start/end date range, then lists every note in '_00 Planer/_01 Dziennik' whose filename starts with a date inside that range.
behaviour_notes: Handles year rollover for weeks spanning Dec/Jan (endYear = year+1 if end month < start month) (lines 122-123).
