External dependency on the Dataview plugin being installed/enabled; without it this block renders as a raw code fence.
edge_cases: Hardcodes the daily folder path; if the daily folder ever moves, this block breaks independently of the frontmatter-driven month template's dataview query.

capabilities.name: Weekly note embeds Bases 'Created/Updated this week' views
capabilities.description: Embeds two views from Weekly Notes.base ('Created this week', 'Updated this week'), which independently parse the weekly note's own filename to derive its date range and filter all vault files (excluding planner/template/archive folders) by file.ctime/file.mtime.
behaviour_notes: 'Updated this week' is documented in the base file itself as unreliable for past weeks, since file.mtime is a single timestamp, not history (Weekly Notes.base:36-38).

capabilities.name: Rename/move monthly (personal) note to canonical form
capabilities.description: Parses YYYY-MM from the title, computes the canonical 'YYYY-MM MMMM' title, renames the file if needed, and moves it into '_00 Planer/_03 Miesiące'.
behaviour_notes: Writes frontmatter/body content before doing rename/move, commented as 'less fragile' (lines 44-45).

capabilities.name: Monthly note frontmatter + prev/next + Stuff checklist
capabilities.description: Writes 'relates to' link to the paired Work-monthly note, year link, journal/journal-monthly tags, prev/next month links, and a blank '# Stuff' checklist item.

capabilities.name: Monthly note's dataview lists of its weekly/daily notes
capabilities.description: Two plain Dataview LIST queries filter '_00 Planer/_02 Tygodnie' and '_00 Planer/_01 Dziennik' for notes whose frontmatter 'month' field contains a link to this monthly note, sorted ascending by filename.
behaviour_notes: Comment explains this is link-driven (frontmatter 'month') rather than file.ctime-driven, so a month note created in advance still correctly lists its own future notes (Monthly Periodic Template.md:58-60).
edge_cases: Depends entirely on the daily/weekly templates having actually written the 'month' frontmatter link; a manually created daily/weekly note without it won't show up.

capabilities.name: Monthly note embeds Bases 'Created/Updated this month' views
capabilities.description: Embeds 'Created this month' / 'Updated this month' views from Weekly Notes.base, which derive the month's date range from the host note's own filename (YYYY-MM prefix).

capabilities.name: Monthly-Work template only activates on a matching title
capabilities.description: Requires the title to start with 'YYYY-MM' AND end with ' - Work'; if either check fails, the template returns immediately and writes nothing, since it is auto-triggered on every new file in the Work-monthly folder regardless of name.
behaviour_notes: In-file comment: 'Apply only when rules pass => do nothing' — a deliberate no-op guard, not an error path (lines 41-43).
edge_cases: A file created in '_00 Planer/_03a Miesiące Work' with a non-conforming name is auto-templated to an empty file with no warning.

capabilities.name: Monthly-Work frontmatter, Plan/Links/TODO sections
capabilities.description: Writes monthly/work tags, 'relates to' link back to the personal monthly note and '1on1 start here', year link, prev/next Work-month links, and static Plan/Ważne linki/TODO section stubs (including a hardcoded Notion URL).
edge_cases: Hardcoded Notion link and 1on1 note names are copy-pasted content, not computed — will go stale independent of the template logic.

capabilities.name: Pre-generate one heading per weekday of the month
capabilities.description: Walks backward from end-of-month to start-of-month, emitting '## DD.MM, dddd' for each day whose isoWeekday() <= 5 (Mon-Fri), producing a descending list of weekday headings under '# <u>Daily</u>'.
behaviour_notes: Weekends are never given headings, which is exactly why the daily template's anchored-link feature finds no heading (and links nothing) on Sat/Sun.

capabilities.name: Monthly-Work note embeds Bases Work-filtered month views
capabilities.description: Embeds 'Created this month (Work)' / 'Updated this month (Work)' views, which additionally filter to notes whose 'categories' frontmatter links to '[[Work]]', on top of the same filename-derived month range.
behaviour_notes: In-file comment notes the title prefix ('YYYY-MM MMMM - Work') shares slice offsets with the plain monthly title, so the same slice(0,4)/slice(5,7) logic works unmodified (Weekly Notes.base:101-103).

capabilities.name: Create a yearly note (static frontmatter only)
capabilities.description: Applies a fixed frontmatter block (journal, journal/yearly tags) with no computed logic, rename, or move — the only granularity whose template does no scripting at all.
behaviour_notes: Unlike day/week/month, periodic-notes-anks.calendarSets[0].year has allowPrefixMatch:false and a bare 'YYYY' format, so no rename step is needed — the note is already created with its final name.

capabilities.name: Prefer a side-installed dev plugin over its community-store copy
capabilities.description: Every cross-plugin lookup across the three forks tries a side-installed dev-build plugin id first ('periodic-notes-anks', 'calendar-anks') before falling back to the community-store id ('periodic-notes', 'calendar'). This lets a locally built dev copy of Periodic Notes/Calendar coexist with the store copy and still be recognized by every settings getter and feature-availability check in all three plugins.
behaviour_notes: dni-settings.getPeriodicNotesPlugin() is exported (since bba664e) and re-exported from dni-index; obsidian-calendar-plugin does NOT import it, it keeps its own duplicate copy of the same lookup in ocp-settings.

The dev id is hardcoded per file as the literal string 'periodic-notes-anks' / 'calendar-anks' in three separate places; a merge must keep this id (or make it configurable) in every place or dev-build detection silently breaks in whichever copy was missed.

History across commits: be90253 first applied the fallback to daily/weekly checks and the calendar lookup in dni; 7727890 applied the same fix to ocp's own periodic-notes lookup; bba664e finally closed the gap for dni's monthly/quarterly/yearly checks, which be90253 had missed.
edge_cases: If both a dev and a store copy of periodic-notes/calendar are installed, the dev copy always wins; there is no user-facing way to prefer the store copy.

capabilities.name: Prefix-match fallback for weekly note filenames (daily-notes-interface)
capabilities.description: obsidian-daily-notes-interface's getDateFromFilename() accepts a weekly note filename that only starts with (a prefix of) the configured moment format, not just an exact match, when the weekly settings' allowPrefixMatch flag is true. E.g. a file named '2026-W07, 09.02 - 15.02.md' resolves against format 'gggg-[W]ww'.
behaviour_notes: allowPrefixMatch is read off IPeriodicNoteSettings (dni-types), populated in getWeeklyNoteSettings() from Periodic Notes' weekly settings; always false when the settings source is the Calendar plugin's own (non-periodic-notes) weekly config, since Calendar has no such field.

ocp's revealActiveNote() was fixed in commit 7727890 to call getDateFromFile(file, 'week') instead of an inline strict-only moment() parse, so 'reveal active note' now also works for a prefix-matched weekly note; before that fix the note correctly showed as a dot on the calendar but jump-to-note failed for it.

Only tries the single format resolved for the requested granularity, and preserves the pre-existing ambiguous-week-format special case (isFormatAmbiguous) only in the exact-match branch. This differs from obsidian-periodic-notes' own getDateWithPrefixFallback(), which loops over every possible format and has no ambiguous-format handling. The two implementations are independent and can diverge (see observations).
edge_cases: An ambiguous week-only format (e.g. one using only 'W'/'w' tokens) is only disambiguated on exact match; the prefix-match branch does not apply the same disambiguation.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity 'Allow prefix matching' toggle (Periodic Notes)
capabilities.description: obsidian-periodic-notes gets a new opt-in toggle per calendar-set granularity ('Allow prefix matching'). When enabled, PeriodicNotesCache.resolve() accepts a file whose name only starts with the configured format, via the new getDateWithPrefixFallback() helper, instead of requiring an exact filename match.
behaviour_notes: getDateWithPrefixFallback tries every possible format (getPossibleFormats) strictly first, then loosely; a loose match is only accepted if the reformatted date is a string-prefix of the input filename.

cache.ts records matchData.exact = isExactMatch, so a prefix-matched note is cached as a non-exact match (existing frontmatter-vs-filename priority logic elsewhere in resolve() already branches on match type/exactness).
Default is false (src/settings/index.ts:56 and src/types.ts:24), so existing vaults are unaffected until a user opts in per granularity.
edge_cases: This is a separate, independently written implementation from daily-notes-interface's weekly-only prefix match; see the duplication observation.

capabilities.name: Open/create the month's periodic note by clicking the calendar month header
capabilities.description: In the Calendar sidebar, clicking the month header (the 'h3.title' element, e.g. 'Oct 2026') opens or creates that month's periodic note via the Periodic Notes plugin's openPeriodicNote('month', ...) API, instead of only resetting the calendar view to the current month. Meta-click (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) opens it in a new split.
behaviour_notes: Registered as a capture-phase click listener on the view's contentEl (src/view.ts:136-141) so it runs before obsidian-calendar-ui's own bubble-phase h3.title handler (resetDisplayedMonth); when this handler can act it calls preventDefault/stopPropagation so the library's reset does not also fire for the same click.

Falls through to the existing reset-to-current-month behavior whenever Periodic Notes is missing, monthly notes are disabled/unavailable, or the displayed month can't be read from Calendar.svelte -- i.e. purely additive over upstream behavior, never a hard replacement.

getMonthlyNotesPeriodicNotesPlugin() (ocp-settings) was buggy when first introduced in commit 5ed4307: it read periodicNotes.settings.monthly, but settings is a Svelte writable store, not a plain object, so the check always evaluated to undefined/falsy and the function always returned null -- the whole feature never actually fired. Fixed one commit later (39040cd) to check the plugin's calendarSetManager.getActiveGranularities() instead, with fail-closed behavior if that API is unavailable, and to also verify openPeriodicNote exists before returning the plugin instance.
obsidian-calendar-ui stays pinned at its existing version for this feature; no changes were made to it.
edge_cases: If calendarSetManager or getActiveGranularities() is absent on the installed Periodic Notes build, the feature silently disables itself (fails closed) instead of risking an openPeriodicNote/createPeriodicNote call for a granularity that might be disabled or unconfigured.

capabilities.name: Periodic Notes settings tab no longer crashes on Obsidian 1.13+
capabilities.description: Periodic Notes' settings detail pane no longer throws when Obsidian's settings-modal DOM lacks a '.vertical-tab-content' element at mount time (a DOM change introduced in Obsidian 1.13). Previously this threw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading scroll)', with a follow-on 'Cannot read properties of null (reading insertBefore)', leaving the Svelte settings pane half-mounted.
behaviour_notes: The fix is a single optional-chaining operator (`?.scroll(0, 0)`) turning a hard crash into a no-op when the element is missing.

capabilities.name: obsidian-daily-notes-interface self-builds when installed as a git dependency
capabilities.description: package.json's new 'prepare' script (rollup -c) runs automatically after yarn/npm clones this package as a git dependency, so dist/main.js (the package's declared 'main' entry) exists before it is linked into a consumer's node_modules. Without it, a git-URL install ships only TypeScript sources and breaks any consumer that resolves the built output.
behaviour_notes: Exists specifically because obsidian-calendar-plugin now consumes this package via a github:matisnape/... pinned dependency rather than a published npm release.

observations.why_it_matters: Any merged code path that routes through the generic dispatcher (rather than calling create*Note directly) will throw a TypeError for quarter/year instead of creating a note. A naive merge that keeps this dispatcher as 'the' generic entry point silently breaks two of the five granularities.

observations.what: The 'try dev plugin id ("periodic-notes-anks"), then production id ("periodic-notes")' probe is implemented twice: once as the shared getPeriodicNotesPlugin() in settings.ts (used by settings.ts itself and by the monthly/quarterly/yearly plugin-detection functions), and once inlined separately inside appHasDailyNotesPluginLoaded and appHasWeeklyNotesPluginLoaded in index.ts, which do not call getPeriodicNotesPlugin() at all. The Calendar plugin's 'calendar-anks'/'calendar' probe (index.ts:38-39) is also unique to appHasWeeklyNotesPluginLoaded and not centralized anywhere.
observations.why_it_matters: A merge that only updates the shared getPeriodicNotesPlugin() helper (e.g. to add a third plugin id, or change probe order) will miss the two inlined copies in index.ts, silently leaving daily/weekly detection out of sync with monthly/quarterly/yearly.

observations.what: The {{date±N unit:format}}/{{time}} regex-and-callback used to fill in date/time template tokens is copy-pasted verbatim across createDailyNote, createWeeklyNote, createMonthlyNote, createQuarterlyNote, and createYearlyNote instead of being a shared helper.
observations.why_it_matters: A fix or extension to this token syntax (e.g. adding a new unit or fixing a formatting edge case) has to be applied identically in five places; the merge should extract this into one shared function up front rather than porting all five copies.

observations.what: getAllDailyNotes() does not call appHasDailyNotesPluginLoaded() before walking the vault, unlike getAllWeeklyNotes/getAllMonthlyNotes/getAllQuarterlyNotes/getAllYearlyNotes, which all return {} early if their respective plugin isn't enabled.
observations.why_it_matters: If daily notes are effectively 'disabled' but a folder still exists at the configured (possibly stale/default) path, getAllDailyNotes will still scan it and throw DailyNotesFolderMissingError only if the folder is truly absent — it never short-circuits the way the other four granularities do. A merge that unifies getAll*Notes into one generic function must decide whether to add the missing guard to daily or intentionally drop it from the others.

observations.what: allowPrefixMatch is declared generically on IPeriodicNoteSettings and consumed generically in parse.ts's getDateFromFilename for every granularity, but only getWeeklyNoteSettings ever populates it (and only from the Periodic Notes plugin path — the Calendar-plugin fallback hardcodes it to false). getDailyNoteSettings/getMonthlyNoteSettings/getQuarterlyNoteSettings/getYearlyNoteSettings never include the key at all.
observations.why_it_matters: Prefix/loose filename matching (e.g. matching '2026-01-15 Some Title.md' as a daily note) silently cannot work for day/month/quarter/year notes today, even though nothing in parse.ts's logic is week-specific. If the merge wants to offer prefix matching uniformly, each of the four other resolve-*-settings functions needs the same wiring added.

observations.what: Weekly-note detection (appHasWeeklyNotesPluginLoaded) treats the mere presence of the Calendar plugin as sufficient ('true' as soon as app.plugins.getPlugin('calendar-anks'||'calendar') returns truthy), without checking any 'weekly enabled' flag on it — whereas daily notes check internalPlugins...['daily-notes'].enabled, and monthly/quarterly/yearly check periodicNotes.settings[g].enabled. Weekly is the only granularity where plugin-installed implies feature-enabled.
observations.why_it_matters: A user who has the Calendar plugin installed but has turned off its weekly-notes feature (if such a toggle exists) will still be reported as 'weekly notes enabled' by this library — a behavior a unified implementation should decide to keep or fix explicitly, not inherit by accident.

observations.what: The repo-root index.d.ts (hand-maintained, not referenced by package.json's missing 'types' field, and not produced by the rollup build which only emits dist/main.js) is out of sync with src/: it declares DailyNotesFolderMissingError/WeeklyNotesFolderMissingError/MonthlyNotesFolderMissingError/QuarterlyNotesFolderMissingError/YearlyNotesFolderMissingError as top-level exports of the package, but src/index.ts never imports or re-exports any of the five *FolderMissingError classes from daily.ts/weekly.ts/monthly.ts/quarterly.ts/yearly.ts. It also declares IPeriodicNoteSettings without allowPrefixMatch, unlike src/types.ts.
observations.why_it_matters: Anyone consulting index.d.ts for 'what this library exports' (rather than reading src/index.ts) will believe the *FolderMissingError classes and a narrower settings shape are part of the public API; a merge should treat src/index.ts as the sole source of truth and either delete or regenerate index.d.ts.

observations.what: Despite the role hint that obsidian-periodic-notes 'historically' used this library, the checked-out obsidian-periodic-notes repo does not import 'obsidian-daily-notes-interface' anywhere and is not listed in its package.json dependencies; it instead ships its own independent parser.ts, cache.ts, calendarSetManager.ts, and settings/ implementing equivalent (but not necessarily identical) date-parsing and settings-resolution logic.
observations.why_it_matters: The merge cannot treat obsidian-daily-notes-interface as periodic-notes' current settings/parsing implementation — that logic has diverged into a second, independently-evolved copy that must be diffed against this one (parse.ts especially) rather than assumed compatible. This should be resolved by whichever agent maps obsidian-periodic-notes.

observations.what: getPeriodicNotesPlugin() is exported from settings.ts and imported into index.ts, but is not included in index.ts's final `export { ... }` block, so it is not part of the package's public API even though three of the five plugin-detection functions (monthly/quarterly/yearly) are effectively thin wrappers around it.
observations.why_it_matters: A consumer plugin cannot get the raw Periodic Notes plugin instance (e.g. to read settings for a custom granularity, or to react to its own onload) without reimplementing the dev/production id probe itself — worth deciding whether to make this a first-class public export in the merged library.

observations.what: weekly.ts, monthly.ts, quarterly.ts, and yearly.ts each import their corresponding appHasXNotesPluginLoaded function from './index' (the package's own aggregator module), creating an internal circular dependency (index.ts imports from these files' create/get functions, and they import back from index.ts for the plugin-detection function).
observations.why_it_matters: This works today because TypeScript/ES module circular imports of pure functions are tolerated, but a restructure during the merge (e.g. splitting index.ts differently, or bundling with stricter tooling) could break at the module-resolution level; the merge should relocate appHasXNotesPluginLoaded next to detect-periodic-notes-plugin in a settings/detection module instead of index.ts to remove the cycle.

observations.what: Calendar.svelte's public prop contract was fully rewritten between 0.3.12 and 0.4.0. 0.3.12 exposes six named callback props (onHoverDay, onHoverWeek, onClickDay, onClickWeek, onContextMenuDay, onContextMenuWeek) plus three exported navigation functions (incrementDisplayedMonth, decrementDisplayedMonth, resetDisplayedMonth) and a plain reassignable `export let displayedMonth`. 0.4.0 replaces the six callbacks with one `eventHandlers: CallableFunction[]` array spread onto children (new signature: (granularity, date, file, ...) instead of (date, isMetaPressed)), adds required `plugin: Plugin` and `getSourceSettings` props, removes the three exported nav functions entirely (moved to Nav.svelte, not exposed to the parent), and moves displayedMonth into an internal context store that the exported `displayedMonth` prop is never written back to.
observations.why_it_matters: The real consumer's wrapper (obsidian-calendar-plugin/src/ui/Calendar.svelte) does `bind:displayedMonth` on CalendarBase and relies on that binding for view.ts's `getDisplayedMonth()` (used to open the correct monthly note) and for its own midnight-rollover heartbeat check. In 0.4.0 that bind silently stops tracking navigation (no runtime error, just a stale value) because the exported prop is only used to seed the internal store once.

observations.what: ICalendarSource / IDayMetadata / IDot were fully rewritten. 0.3.12: ICalendarSource = {getDailyMetadata?, getWeeklyMetadata?} each returning {classes?, dataAttributes?, dots?}; IDot = {className, color, isFilled}. 0.4.0: ICalendarSource = {id, name, description?, getMetadata?(granularity, date, file), defaultSettings, registerSettings?} returning IEvaluatedMetadata {value, goal?, dots, attrs?}; IDot = {isFilled} only (color now lives on ISourceSettings, applied by the parent, not the source).
observations.why_it_matters: All four of the plugin's real sources (streak, tasks, wordCount, tags in obsidian-calendar-plugin/src/ui/sources/) implement the old getDailyMetadata/getWeeklyMetadata shape verbatim, returning {classes, dots} with IDot {className, color, isFilled}. Porting 0.4.0 wholesale means every source needs a full rewrite (add id/name/defaultSettings, switch to getMetadata(granularity, date, file), change dots to {isFilled} only, move color out to settings) — this is new source code, not a mechanical prop rename.

observations.what: The clickable month-header DOM structure changed. 0.3.12's Nav.svelte renders `<h3 class="title" on:click={resetDisplayedMonth}>`. 0.4.0 moves the title into the new Month.svelte as a non-heading `<div>` (with the on:click/on:contextmenu handlers) wrapping an inner `<span class="title">` used only for styling.
observations.why_it_matters: obsidian-calendar-plugin/src/view.ts's onMonthHeaderClick intercepts capture-phase clicks with `target.closest('h3.title')` specifically because 0.3.12's Calendar has no month-level click prop at all. That selector will never match 0.4.0's markup (no <h3> anywhere), silently disabling 'click month header to open the monthly note'. Meanwhile 0.4.0 ships a native onClick/onContextMenu path for the month header via eventHandlers, but the plugin's current wrapper (src/ui/Calendar.svelte) never threads any handler for granularity 'month' through at all — the merge needs to pick one mechanism, not keep both half-wired.

observations.what: Month-granularity support (fileStore.ts, Month.svelte's metadata/popover path, the 'month' branch throughout) does not exist in 0.3.12 at all — there is no fileStore.ts, and ICalendarSource never mentions month. It is entirely new in 0.4.0.
observations.why_it_matters: obsidian-calendar-plugin currently implements its own monthly-note handling directly in src/view.ts/src/io (via getMonthlyNotesPeriodicNotesPlugin), independent of calendar-ui. Merging in 0.4.0's native month support is new functionality that can conflict or duplicate with the plugin's existing monthly-note code path, not just a drop-in upgrade.

observations.what: obsidian-daily-notes-interface is pinned at 0.8.4 for the 0.3.12 line vs 0.9.2 for 0.4.0. fileStore.ts (0.4.0-only) imports getAllMonthlyNotes and appHasMonthlyNotesPluginLoaded from that package.
observations.why_it_matters: Bumping this transitive dependency is a prerequisite for merging in the 0.4.0 fileStore/month code, not optional — the 0.8.4 API surface almost certainly lacks the monthly-note helpers 0.4.0 depends on.

observations.what: The reset-to-today control lost its localized text label. 0.3.12's Nav.svelte showed `today.calendar().split(/\d|\s/)[0]` (a locale-aware word, e.g. the translated 'Today'). 0.4.0's reset button is icon-only (a filled Dot) with a hardcoded English aria-label 'Reset to current month'.
observations.why_it_matters: This vault runs primarily in Polish; a straight merge silently drops the localized 'Dzisiaj'-style label users currently see, replacing it with an icon plus an English-only tooltip.

observations.what: The `localeData` prop on Calendar (and the `today`/`localeData` arguments threaded through to getDaysOfWeek/getMonth) has no real effect: both utils.ts functions declare only the parameters they use, then swallow everything else via `..._args: unknown[]`, and read only the global `window.moment()` state. This is identical in both 0.3.12 and 0.4.0 (utils.ts is byte-for-byte the same).
observations.why_it_matters: Anyone porting or extending this code could reasonably assume passing a different `localeData` to Calendar changes week start/weekday names for that instance; it does not — only a prior call to configureGlobalMomentLocale() (which mutates the shared global) has any effect. Worth fixing (either wire the param through or remove it) rather than carrying the dead parameter into the merged repo.

observations.what: Arrow.svelte reads `(window.app as any).isMobile` directly instead of using the IS_MOBILE Svelte context that Calendar.svelte sets and that Day.svelte/PopoverMenu.svelte both consume.
observations.why_it_matters: Harmless today (same global either way, since Calendar always sets context to `plugin.app.isMobile`), but it's an inconsistent pattern within the same 0.4.0 codebase and worth normalizing when merging so mobile-detection has one source of truth.

observations.what: MetadataResolver.svelte gained a pending-state branch in 0.4.0: `{#await metadata}` now renders `<slot metadata={null}/>` while the promise is in flight. 0.3.12's version has no `{#await}` pending branch at all (only `{:then}`), so it renders nothing until the promise resolves.
observations.why_it_matters: 0.4.0 cells will render their 'no metadata yet' state (e.g. empty dots) briefly on every recompute, then flash to the resolved state, where 0.3.12 rendered nothing until resolved. Minor but real visual/behavioral difference to be aware of when comparing screenshots or writing tests across the two versions.

observations.what: obsidian-calendar-plugin re-implements calui's unexported isMetaPressed helper verbatim, with a comment acknowledging it: 'Mirrors obsidian-calendar-ui's (unexported) isMetaPressed helper so meta-click behaves the same on the month header as it does on day/week cells.'
observations.why_it_matters: calui never exports isMetaPressed from index.ts even though it's simple, stable, and needed by any host implementing month-header handling itself (as the 0.3.12-era plugin does). Exporting it in the merged library removes a real, currently-necessary duplication.

observations.what: Month-header click now opens/creates the month's Periodic Notes note (capture-phase interceptor + fail-closed plugin resolution), instead of only resetting the calendar to today. This is entirely absent upstream.
observations.why_it_matters: Easy to lose silently in a merge/rebase: it's a capture-phase DOM listener racing an upstream bubble-phase handler, plus a new exported Svelte accessor and a new settings.ts function, all introduced across commits 5ed4307 and 39040cd. A naive merge that only carries forward file-level diffs on view.ts could easily drop the Calendar.svelte accessor or the capture/bubble ordering comment, silently breaking the feature or corrupting event handling on the month header for everyone.

observations.what: appHasPeriodicNotesPluginLoaded() (src/settings.ts:48-56) reads `periodicNotes.settings?.weekly?.enabled` directly off the plugin instance. The sibling function getMonthlyNotesPeriodicNotesPlugin()'s own commit message (39040cd) states that `periodicNotes.settings` is actually a Svelte store (Writable<ISettings>), not a plain object -- which is exactly why the monthly check had to be rewritten to use calendarSetManager instead. The weekly check was never fixed the same way and may always read undefined.
observations.why_it_matters: If true, `showWeeklyNote`'s legacy settings UI and the 'Open Weekly Note' command's checkCallback may never correctly detect an active Periodic Notes weekly setup, always falling back to this plugin's own (deprecated) weekly-note path even when Periodic Notes is properly configured. Worth verifying against a live Periodic Notes instance before porting this function as-is.

observations.what: This plugin's obsidian-daily-notes-interface dependency was repointed across 3 commits (8e2545b, 102ad6d, dc780c0) from the published npm version 0.9.0 to a personal fork (matisnape/obsidian-daily-notes-interface) pinned at commit bba664e424b962f989a2a4fc70ad882ee489f588 via a GitHub dependency spec, specifically to get allowPrefixMatch / dev-id plugin detection behavior that upstream obsidian-daily-notes-interface doesn't have.
observations.why_it_matters: If the merged obsidian-calendaric repo consolidates on a different obsidian-daily-notes-interface source (e.g. the community version, or a different fork mapped by another agent), this plugin's getDateFromFile/allowPrefixMatch-dependent behavior (see jump-calendar-to-active-note fix) and its dev-id plugin detection pattern may silently regress unless that same fork's changes are ported into whichever DNI implementation is chosen as canonical.

observations.what: openOrCreateDailyNote() looks up and applies `app.vault.getConfig('defaultViewMode')` when opening an existing note (src/view.ts:367-372), but openOrCreateWeeklyNote() does not (src/view.ts:339-342) -- it just calls `leaf.openFile(existingFile)` with no options.
observations.why_it_matters: An existing weekly note may open in a different edit/preview mode than the user's configured default, unlike daily notes. Worth deciding intentionally when porting rather than carrying the asymmetry forward silently.

observations.what: weeklyNoteFormat, weeklyNoteTemplate, and weeklyNoteFolder are declared in ISettings, given defaults, and editable via the settings tab, but nothing in this repo's source ever reads them -- createWeeklyNote(date) (obsidian-daily-notes-interface) is called with only a date argument.
observations.why_it_matters: A user who fills these fields expecting them to control weekly note creation gets no effect; they were presumably superseded by Periodic Notes' own settings. A merge should either wire them up or drop them rather than porting dead settings forward.

observations.what: Two separate functions in settings.ts (appHasPeriodicNotesPluginLoaded and getMonthlyNotesPeriodicNotesPlugin) each independently implement the same 'try periodic-notes-anks, then periodic-notes' plugin-id probe.
observations.why_it_matters: A future dev-plugin-id change (or a third id) has to be updated in two places; this already caused one missed-gap bugfix (commit 7727890) when the id probe was added to only one of the two functions initially.

observations.what: onHoverDay/onHoverWeek trigger the 'link-hover' workspace event with `note?.path` even when no note exists for the hovered date, passing an undefined path.
observations.why_it_matters: Whatever hover-preview consumer Obsidian core wires up may attempt to preview `undefined`, showing an empty or erroring popover instead of no popover at all. Minor UX rough edge worth deciding on when porting.

observations.what: getDateUIDFromFile() only compares the file's basename against daily/weekly formats and explicitly does not check the file's folder path (own TODO comment: '// TODO: I'm not checking the path!').
observations.why_it_matters: Two same-named files in different folders (e.g. a manually created note that happens to match the daily-note date format, outside the daily notes folder) would be indistinguishable by this lookup, potentially mis-highlighting the wrong file as 'active' in the calendar.

observations.what: Local fork guards the settings-tab scroll call against a missing '.vertical-tab-content' element.
observations.why_it_matters: Obsidian 1.13 changed the settings-modal DOM; without the optional-chaining guard, opening the plugin's settings tab throws ('Cannot read properties of undefined (reading scroll)') and leaves the Svelte component half-mounted, breaking the whole settings UI. A merge must carry this guard forward or the crash reappears on current Obsidian.

observations.what: Local fork adds an 'allowPrefixMatch' setting and its whole vertical slice.
observations.why_it_matters: Not present upstream (liamcain/obsidian-periodic-notes). A merge that starts from upstream code will silently lose prefix-matching for notes whose filenames only start with the configured format (e.g. weekly notes with a trailing date-range suffix).

observations.what: Local fork replaced a bare JSON module import with fs.readFileSync + JSON.parse in the esbuild config, and pinned Node 24.12.0.
observations.why_it_matters: Node 24 rejects an unattributed JSON module import (ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING); without this change the build breaks on the fork's own pinned toolchain. A merged build script for the whole family must pick one convention for reading manifest.json, and honor (or explicitly override) the Node version pin.

observations.what: Local fork dropped 'yarn run lint' from the production build script.
observations.why_it_matters: svelte-check 2.7.0 can't parse this repo's inline type-only import specifiers ('import { type X }'), a pre-existing toolchain mismatch, so the fork bypassed the gate rather than fixing it. A merged repo needs a working lint/typecheck step or will silently reintroduce type errors.

observations.what: Top-level per-granularity settings keys (daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/yearly) exist only inside a private, migration-only type — not in the live settings interface used at runtime.
where: src/calendarSetManager.ts:20-30 (ILegacySettings — has them, but this type is only used by isLegacySettings()/migrateLegacySettingsToCalendarSet(), called exactly once from src/main.ts:177-187 during loadSettings())
observations.why_it_matters: A merge that assumes v0.0.17 still reads/writes top-level daily/weekly/... settings (as much older versions of this plugin, and possibly sibling repos in this family, do) will be targeting dead code. The only live, ongoing config surface in this fork is calendarSets[]; the top-level keys are read exactly once, from raw loaded JSON, purely to detect a pre-upgrade vault.

observations.what: The Locale dropdown in the settings dashboard writes its value to the wrong Obsidian vault-config key.
observations.why_it_matters: Both the 'Start week on' and 'Locale' dropdowns call app.vault.setConfig('weekStart', val) — the Locale handler is a copy-paste of the week-start handler and never writes 'localeOverride'. Changing Locale in the UI never actually persists a locale override (it just re-writes weekStart with the locale-dropdown's value instead), while configureGlobalMomentLocale() at load time correctly reads 'localeOverride' from vault config — so the bug is invisible until you try to change locale live and reload.

observations.what: ISettings carries several fields nothing reads at runtime.
observations.why_it_matters: Declared and defaulted but never read again anywhere else in the source (confirmed by grep). localeOverride/weekStart are additionally shadowed by the real values living in Obsidian's vault-level config, not plugin data.json. A merge should not port these fields as if they carried live state.

observations.what: FileOptionsSwitcher, PeriodicNoteCreateModal and IconButton.svelte are defined but never instantiated or imported anywhere in the source.
where: src/modal.ts:27-74 (PeriodicNoteCreateModal class only — showFileMenu in the same file IS used)
observations.why_it_matters: None of the three is reachable from any command, event, or component in this repo (confirmed by grep for each class/component name). Do not port these as capabilities; they are inert leftovers — fileOptionsSwitcher.ts's own 'Delete file' item even has an empty onChooseSuggestion body.

observations.what: MatchType's 'date-prefixed' variant is declared but never produced.
observations.why_it_matters: Only 'filename' and 'frontmatter' are ever assigned to matchData.matchType anywhere in the source. Harmless, but a porting agent should not build logic that expects this variant to occur.

observations.what: Frontmatter-based note resolution ignores the calendar set's configured format and its allowPrefixMatch flag, unlike the filename-based path.
observations.why_it_matters: resolve() (filename matching) correctly uses getPossibleFormats() + getDateWithPrefixFallback() against the user's configured format. resolveChangedMetadata() (frontmatter matching) instead hard-codes DEFAULT_FORMAT[granularity] for the strict parse. A note identified only via frontmatter (e.g. `day: 2022-02-02`) with a non-default format configured will silently fail to resolve. A merged note-resolution engine should unify these two code paths rather than keep the asymmetry.

observations.what: The vault-wide loose date-fallback in cache.resolve() is not scoped to any calendar set's configured folder.
observations.why_it_matters: When no active granularity's folder+format matches a file, resolve() falls through to getLooselyMatchedDate(file.basename) with no folder check at all. Any markdown file anywhere in the vault whose basename merely contains a YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM/YYYY-shaped substring (e.g. '2026 Meeting Notes.md') gets cached as an inexact match for every calendar set that has active granularities, which can surface as incorrect '+N related notes' badges and pollute the related-files switcher with unrelated files.

observations.what: No monkey-patching of Obsidian's built-in Quick Switcher exists anywhere in src/switcher/*; the real hazard is the stateful hand-off between two custom modals.
observations.why_it_matters: A grep for prototype/monkey/patch/QuickSwitcher across src/ found nothing. All four 'switcher' classes are independent SuggestModal/FuzzySuggestModal subclasses (Obsidian's own public modal API), opened from the plugin's own commands — not modifications of core UI. The actual merge hazard is the Tab hand-off between NLDNavigator and RelatedFilesSwitcher (closing one modal, opening the other, and replaying the query string via a synthetic 'input' event) — that chain has no test coverage and is easy to break silently if either constructor's signature changes during a merge.

observations.what: The assignment's description of where openPeriodicNote/getDateWithPrefixFallback live doesn't match the code exactly.
observations.why_it_matters: openPeriodicNote is a PeriodicNotesPlugin method in main.ts, not utils.ts. utils.ts does correctly hold getDateWithPrefixFallback and the rest of the date/template helpers. Noted so a porting agent doesn't waste time searching utils.ts for openPeriodicNote.

observations.what: getPeriodicNotes' own author flags its shape as unsettled.
where: src/main.ts:239 (inline comment: '// TODO: What API do I want for this?')
observations.why_it_matters: Treat this method's signature (a boolean includeFinerGranularities flag) as a redesign candidate in the merged plugin rather than a contract that must be preserved exactly.

observations.what: Cross-plugin lookup by manifest id will fail for this specific vault install.
observations.why_it_matters: The assignment states this fork is installed under the dev plugin id 'periodic-notes-anks'. Any other plugin (e.g. obsidian-calendar-plugin) calling app.plugins.getPlugin('periodic-notes') gets undefined in this vault, even though the code and its public methods are otherwise present and working. This is an install-time integration risk specific to this vault, not a code bug — worth flagging before testing the merged plugin's cross-plugin API here.

observations.what: Week-start day-of-week helpers are re-implemented three separate times within this one repo.
observations.why_it_matters: Three separate hard-coded ['sunday'..'saturday'] arrays with slightly different rotation logic for locale week-start. A merge across this whole plugin family should consolidate on one canonical day-of-week utility rather than porting all three independently.

observations.what: All UI in this repo (settings tab, calendar grid, modal) is plain TypeScript building DOM nodes by hand (createEl/createDiv/addEventListener), not Svelte. The three source repos this is merging (Calendar plugin, Periodic Notes plugin, and presumably shared helpers) are Svelte-based.
observations.why_it_matters: The old Svelte components cannot be copied into this repo's DOM-based UI. This records a technology difference, not a blocked requirement: a from-scratch rewrite was always going to re-implement the views. Choose the new UI boundary deliberately and preserve behaviour, not either repository's component structure.

observations.what: Only 'day' and 'week' granularities are functionally implemented anywhere: createNote's type signature is 'day' | 'week' only, the settings UI only renders real controls (format/folder/template/openAtStartup/enabled) for day and week, and month/quarter/year exist solely as PeriodicConfig data shapes with permanently-disabled placeholder toggles in the UI.
observations.why_it_matters: This is the single most important fact for the port plan: month, quarter, and year note creation/opening/templating/dots/settings-UI all still need to be built from scratch, even though the data shape (PeriodicConfig, DEFAULT_SETTINGS.month/quarter/year) already exists.

observations.what: docs/guide.md explicitly states 'Week tokens are resolved using the same week-start locale as your "Start week on" setting', but formatWithWeekTokens/applyWeekTokens hard-code ISO weekday numbering (Monday=1..Sunday=7) via WEEKDAY_ISO, completely independent of the weekStart setting.
observations.why_it_matters: A user who sets 'Start week on: Sunday' will still get {{monday:...}} always meaning ISO Monday, not the first day of their configured week — the documented behaviour and the implemented behaviour disagree. When porting/fixing, decide (and test) which one is correct rather than assuming the doc is accurate.

observations.what: The 'Format & template guide' link in settings opens docs/guide.md via `(window as any).require('electron').shell.openPath(...)`, an Electron/desktop-only API, while manifest.json declares `isDesktopOnly: false`.
observations.why_it_matters: This will throw (window.require is undefined) on Obsidian mobile, contradicting AGENTS.md's 'Avoid Node/Electron APIs if you want mobile compatibility' and the plugin's own manifest claim of mobile support.

observations.what: Daily Notes plugin settings can be imported (renderImportCard / dailyNotesImport.ts), but there is no equivalent import path for the core Periodic Notes plugin's week/month/quarter/year settings.
observations.why_it_matters: The stated goal is to absorb both the Calendar plugin and the Periodic Notes plugin. Users migrating from Periodic Notes (which already has week/month/quarter/year notes configured) currently have no assisted migration path at all — this needs to be built, not just extended.

observations.what: AGENTS.md's 'Split large files' guidance ('If any file exceeds ~200-300 lines, consider breaking it into smaller, focused modules') is already violated by src/settings.ts at 425 lines, which mixes the settings data model, the Daily-Notes-import UI, and the full settings-tab UI in one file.
observations.why_it_matters: Merging in the Svelte-based settings UI/logic from the source repos (which is more feature-rich: month/quarter/year, more granular controls) will make this file worse, not better, unless it's split before or during the merge.

observations.what: tsconfig.json enables most strict-mode flags individually (noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, strictBindCallApply, noImplicitThis, useUnknownInCatchVariables) but does not set the umbrella `"strict": true` that AGENTS.md 'prefers', and is missing strictFunctionTypes / strictPropertyInitialization / alwaysStrict specifically.
observations.why_it_matters: Code merged in from other repos may rely on strictPropertyInitialization or strictFunctionTypes being on (or off) and behave differently once merged into this config; worth reconciling before merge rather than after a type-error pile-up.

observations.what: Test coverage is limited to pure-function modules: noteUtils.ts, templateTokens.ts, calendarUtils.ts, settings.ts's clearStartupNote, and dailyNotesImport.ts. Every DOM/IO-touching module (main.ts, CalendarView.ts, calendar.ts's CalendarWidget, calendarDots.ts's DotScanner, modal.ts, noteCreate.ts, and all of settings.ts's rendering code) has zero test coverage.
observations.why_it_matters: Anything the port touches in these files has no regression safety net today; the __mocks__/obsidian.ts mock is also minimal (Plugin, PluginSettingTab, Setting only) and would need real expansion (TFile, Vault, MetadataCache, Workspace, ItemView, Modal) before these paths could be tested at all.

observations.what: No ribbon icon is registered anywhere in main.ts, even though CalendarView.getIcon() defines one ('calendar'); the command palette is the only way to open the calendar view.
observations.why_it_matters: Source plugins being merged in (the Calendar plugin especially) commonly add a ribbon icon as their primary entry point — a source-parity check should confirm whether a ribbon icon needs to be added here.

observations.what: 'Custom Notes' appears as a disabled placeholder group label in the settings UI (renderPlaceholderGroup) but has no corresponding granularity key, PeriodicConfig, or any other data-model support anywhere in types.ts or settings.ts.
observations.why_it_matters: This is pure UI scaffolding for an entirely unbuilt feature (arbitrary/custom periodic note sets, as in the Periodic Notes plugin) — a port plan should treat it as unstarted, not partially built.

observations.what: Daily-note folder/format/template is independently configured in three places: periodic-notes-anks.calendarSets[0].day, core .obsidian/daily-notes.json, and Templater's folder_templates entry. All three currently agree.
observations.why_it_matters: A merged plugin has to decide which of these three config surfaces is authoritative for daily notes; picking wrong, or dropping one silently, changes which plugin creates the file and could break the folder-trigger Templater relies on.

observations.what: periodic-notes-anks/data.json keeps stale top-level daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/yearly keys alongside the live calendarSets[0] object, and the top-level 'monthly' key actively disagrees with the live month config: it points to folder '_00 Planer/_03a Miesiące Work' and template 'Monthly work.md' (i.e. the WORK values), while calendarSets[0].month correctly points to '_00 Planer/_03 Miesiące' and 'Monthly Periodic Template.md'.
observations.why_it_matters: Reading the top-level keys instead of calendarSets[] gives a wrong and specifically misleading answer for month (it looks like a valid config, just the wrong one) rather than an obviously-empty one. Any merge tooling that walks the JSON generically must be pointed at calendarSets[], never the legacy top-level block.

observations.what: The base (non-fork) 'periodic-notes' plugin (id 'periodic-notes', not 'periodic-notes-anks') is installed but absent from community-plugins.json, i.e. disabled. Its data.json contains a second calendar set ('Work') whose folders all live under 'Kurs/...', a top-level folder that does not exist anywhere in this vault.
observations.why_it_matters: Fully orphaned config from a prior vault layout; safe to ignore entirely for the merge, but worth flagging so nobody mistakes the 'Work' calendar-set pattern there for a currently-used multi-calendar-set feature.

observations.what: Quarterly notes are disabled and unconfigured (enabled:false, format/folder/templatePath present but empty or default) in the live calendarSets[0].
observations.why_it_matters: Quarterly-note support can be scoped out of (or deprioritized in) the merged plugin's initial feature set — nothing in this vault depends on it.

observations.what: Only one calendar set ('Default') is defined in the live periodic-notes-anks config; multi-calendar-set support (multiple independent day/week/month/year configs, e.g. a 'Work' set) is unused in the active plugin.
observations.why_it_matters: The 'Work' vs personal split in this vault is instead implemented ad hoc via a second physical folder + a separate template + a ' - Work' filename suffix, not via periodic-notes' own multi-calendar-set mechanism. A merge should not assume calendar-sets are how 'Work' notes are actually kept separate here.

observations.what: enableTimelineComplication is true, but no template, dataview query, or note content in the readable files references a timeline view.
observations.why_it_matters: Timeline complication can likely be deprioritized as a feature nobody is observed to use, pending a UI check outside this agent's read scope.

observations.what: Calendar plugin's word-count-based heatmap dot (wordsPerDot) is the only 'dot source' configured; no custom/metadata-based dot source (e.g. a mood or task-count field) appears in any readable config.
observations.why_it_matters: If the merged plugin's calendar view supports pluggable dot sources, only the built-in word-count source needs porting as 'used'; anything more elaborate is unused here.

observations.what: The weekly template, monthly template, and monthly-work template all embed views from a single shared 'Weekly Notes.base' file, and separately the weekly template's dataviewjs block independently hardcodes the daily-notes folder path ('_00 Planer/_01 Dziennik').
observations.why_it_matters: These are two independent couplings to the exact folder names in periodic-notes-anks.calendarSets[0] (daily folder, and each view's filename-parsing assumptions about title format). Renaming any planner folder or filename format in the merged plugin requires updating both the Templater scripts and the Bases file's view filters/parsing offsets in lockstep — there is no shared constant.

observations.what: Five older periodic-note templates ('Weekly Template.md', 'Monthly Template.md', 'Weekly 1.md', 'Monthly Note Template.md', 'Monthly Work Template DEPRECATED.md') sit in the templates folder but are referenced by no live calendarSets templatePath and no templater folder_templates entry.
observations.why_it_matters: Dead weight for the merge — none of their logic needs porting. Confirmed unreferenced by grepping the live config's template paths, not by filename convention alone.

observations.what: 211 of 219 files in '_00 Planer/_01 Dziennik' match the current daily format 'YYYY-MM-DD, dddd'; 7 are legacy bare 'YYYY-MM-DD.md' files from 2022-2024 (predating the current template), and 1 ('2025-10–10, Friday.md') uses an en-dash typo instead of a hyphen in the date.
observations.why_it_matters: A merged plugin's daily-note lookup/parsing (regex anchored on 'YYYY-MM-DD' at the start of the title) will not resolve these 8 files as daily notes; that's consistent with current behavior (the live template's own regex would reject them too) so it is not a regression, just worth confirming intentional.

observations.what: Weekly, monthly, and monthly-work Bases views (and the weekly dataviewjs block) parse the host note's OWN filename via fixed character offsets (e.g. this.file.name.slice(0,4), slice(13,15)) to recover a date range, rather than reading a frontmatter date field.
observations.why_it_matters: This is the tightest possible coupling to exact filename format (pretty weekly title, 'YYYY-MM MMMM' monthly title). Any format change in the merged plugin must recompute every slice offset in this file or these views silently return empty/wrong ranges with no error.

observations.what: '_00 Planer/_04 1on1' is templater-mapped and populated (10 files) but has no corresponding granularity in periodic-notes-anks (quarter is disabled and unused for it); it's a purely Templater-driven periodic mechanism.
observations.why_it_matters: If the merge intends periodic-notes to be the single source of all periodic behaviour, this folder is a real-world counter-example already living outside that model — worth an explicit decision (fold into 'quarter', or leave as a Templater-only convention).

observations.what: appHasPeriodicNotesPluginLoaded() (used by the Calendar plugin's own settings tab to decide whether to show deprecated weekly-note settings) only checked the community-store 'periodic-notes' plugin id. With only a dev-id build installed, it wrongly reported Periodic Notes as absent and kept showing the deprecated weekly-note settings UI.
observations.why_it_matters: If the dev-id fallback is dropped in the merge, any install running only the dev-id Periodic Notes build regresses to showing dead legacy weekly settings, and a user could reconfigure weekly notes in a UI that no longer does anything.

observations.what: revealActiveNote() bypassed the shared date parser for weekly notes, calling an inline strict-only moment(filename, format, true) parse. A weekly note whose filename only prefix-matches its format was correctly indexed and shown as a dot on the calendar, but 'reveal active note' failed to jump to it. Fixed by routing through getDateFromFile(file, "week") instead.
observations.why_it_matters: Dropping this makes 'reveal active note' silently fail for any prefix-matched weekly note, even though the same note is otherwise fully recognized -- an inconsistent, hard-to-notice regression.

observations.what: package.json/yarn.lock originally pinned obsidian-daily-notes-interface via a machine-local git+file:// URL, duplicated in both 'dependencies' and a yarn 'resolutions' block, specifically to force yarn to dedupe the plugin's own direct dependency and the copy obsidian-calendar-ui pulls in transitively onto a single installed instance.
observations.why_it_matters: Documents why the resolutions block exists at all: without it, two divergent copies of obsidian-daily-notes-interface (one carrying the anks fixes, one not) could end up bundled side by side. Superseded in the very next commit by a network-resolvable pin, but the resolutions-block *pattern* must survive.

observations.what: The git+file:// URL for obsidian-daily-notes-interface only resolves on the machine it was authored on. Replaced with a github:matisnape/obsidian-daily-notes-interface#<sha> pinned ref (in both 'dependencies' and 'resolutions') so the repo installs anywhere.
observations.why_it_matters: This is the load-bearing, portable form of the dependency pin. If a merge collapses these into one repo, this specific pin becomes moot -- but until then, dropping it back to a file:// or machine-local path breaks `yarn install` on any other machine or in CI.

observations.what: Pinned Node to 24.12.0 via .tool-versions (mise); the build already worked cleanly on it, this just avoids requiring an older toolchain.
observations.why_it_matters: Build-only convenience; worth carrying into the merged repo's own .tool-versions so contributors don't hit toolchain drift, but nothing breaks at runtime if dropped.

observations.what: Re-pinned the obsidian-daily-notes-interface dependency and resolutions entry from an earlier sha to bba664e, to pick up the monthly/quarterly/yearly dev-id-fallback fix landed in that commit.
observations.why_it_matters: Encodes that bba664e (not an earlier DNI commit) is the authoritative state of obsidian-daily-notes-interface. Merging an older DNI snapshot silently reintroduces the monthly/quarterly/yearly plugin-detection bug that bba664e fixed.

observations.what: New feature: clicking the calendar sidebar's month header (h3.title) opens/creates that month's periodic note via Periodic Notes' openPeriodicNote('month', ...), instead of only resetting the view to the current month. Meta/Ctrl-click opens a new split. Implemented via a capture-phase click listener on the view container plus a new Calendar.svelte export, getDisplayedMonth().
observations.why_it_matters: No upstream code or documentation describes this. Dropping it silently removes a feature users rely on, with no error: it degrades gracefully back to the old reset-to-current-month click, so the loss would not be noticed until someone asks 'where did month-click-to-open go'.

observations.what: getMonthlyNotesPeriodicNotesPlugin() (added in 5ed4307) read periodicNotes.settings.monthly, but 'settings' is a Svelte writable store, not a plain object, so that property access was always undefined and the guard always returned null -- the month-header-click feature from the previous commit never actually fired for any user. Fixed by checking the plugin's public calendarSetManager.getActiveGranularities() instead, failing closed if that API is unavailable, and verifying openPeriodicNote exists before returning the plugin.
observations.why_it_matters: This is the commit that actually makes capability open-monthly-note-from-header work at all. Porting 5ed4307 into a merge without also porting 39040cd ships dead-on-arrival code: the click handler runs but silently no-ops on every click, which is worse than not having the feature because it looks broken rather than absent.

observations.what: New opt-in 'Allow prefix matching' setting per calendar-set granularity in Periodic Notes. PeriodicNotesCache.resolve() now accepts filenames that only start with the configured format via the new getDateWithPrefixFallback(), which tries every possible format for the granularity strictly first, then loosely, requiring the reformatted date to be a prefix of the filename.
observations.why_it_matters: This is the setting the whole allow-prefix-match feature family (this repo and daily-notes-interface) is built around. If dropped, any weekly/monthly/etc. note named with extra suffix text after the date format (e.g. '2026-W07, 09.02 - 15.02.md') silently stops being recognized as a periodic note.

observations.what: Details.svelte's onMount crashed with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading scroll)' (with a follow-on 'Cannot read properties of null (reading insertBefore)' leaving the settings pane half-mounted), because Obsidian 1.13 changed the settings-modal DOM and '.vertical-tab-content' can be absent at mount time. Fixed with optional chaining.
observations.why_it_matters: Without this guard, the Periodic Notes settings tab hard-crashes on Obsidian 1.13+, making the plugin's settings unusable on any currently-shipping Obsidian version. This is a correctness fix, not a cosmetic one.

observations.what: svelte-check 2.7.0 cannot parse inline type-only import specifiers already used in this repo's .svelte files ('import { type X }'), failing the lint step with spurious parser errors even though esbuild compiles the same TS 4.6-valid code fine. Dropped 'yarn run lint &&' from the production build script; lint remains runnable standalone via 'npm run lint'.
observations.why_it_matters: Build-only. If a merge reintroduces a build script that runs lint-before-build (e.g. by copying an older script verbatim), CI/local builds break on a lint false-positive despite correct code.

observations.what: esbuild.config.mjs's bare 'import manifest from "./manifest.json"' fails under Node >=17 without an import attribute (ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING), which this file never had. Replaced with 'JSON.parse(readFileSync("./manifest.json", "utf8"))'. Node pinned to 24.12.0 via .tool-versions.
observations.why_it_matters: Build-only, but a total build failure on modern Node if reverted. Note this differs from how the other two forks avoid the equivalent class of Node-version issue -- neither of them had a bare JSON import to begin with, so this fix pattern is specific to this repo's esbuild setup and won't automatically transfer if the merge consolidates build tooling.

observations.what: New opt-in prefix-match fallback for weekly note filenames in obsidian-daily-notes-interface: getDateFromFilename() retries with a loose (non-strict) moment parse, accepted only if the reformatted date is a prefix of the filename, but only when settings.allowPrefixMatch is true (plumbed from Periodic Notes' weekly settings; always false when the settings source is the Calendar plugin's own non-periodic-notes weekly config).
observations.why_it_matters: This is the parsing primitive both obsidian-calendar-plugin's revealActiveNote() and the Calendar's own weekly-note dot-indexing depend on. It is independent of, and behaviorally different from, obsidian-periodic-notes' own getDateWithPrefixFallback() (see the duplication observation below), so dropping just one of the two implementations changes behavior only for whichever install path used it.

observations.what: obsidian-daily-notes-interface's getDateFromFilename() prefix-match branch and obsidian-periodic-notes' getDateWithPrefixFallback() independently implement the same 'accept a filename that only starts with the format' idea, but differently: daily-notes-interface only tries the single format resolved for the requested granularity and preserves the pre-existing ambiguous-week-format special case (isFormatAmbiguous) only on its exact-match branch; periodic-notes tries every possible format for the granularity (getPossibleFormats) and has no ambiguous-format handling at all.
observations.why_it_matters: A merge that keeps only one implementation changes which weekly filenames resolve for calendar-plugin-only installs (which go through daily-notes-interface, not periodic-notes) versus periodic-notes-driven installs. This is a silent behavior change for edge-case filenames (e.g. ambiguous week-only formats) depending on which implementation is picked as canonical.

observations.what: appHasDailyNotesPluginLoaded(), appHasWeeklyNotesPluginLoaded(), and the Calendar-plugin lookup inside getWeeklyNoteSettings() only checked the community-store plugin ids ('periodic-notes', 'calendar'). With a side-installed dev-id build ('periodic-notes-anks'/'calendar-anks') present instead of the store copy, these wrongly reported daily/weekly notes as unavailable. New getPeriodicNotesPlugin() helper (dev id tried first) is now used by every getter in this file.
observations.why_it_matters: This is the load-bearing plugin-detection fix for running a dev build alongside a store build. Without it, daily/weekly note creation and settings resolution silently use the wrong (or no) settings source across every consumer of this library.

observations.what: package.json had no 'prepare' script; npm/yarn only ran 'build' (lint + rollup) on an explicit invocation, not automatically after a git-URL clone. A consumer installing this package via a github: dependency (as obsidian-calendar-plugin now does) got only TypeScript sources with no dist/main.js, breaking module resolution entirely. Added 'prepare': 'rollup -c'.
observations.why_it_matters: Not a runtime behavior change but a total install-breaker for any git-URL consumer under the current multi-repo setup. Becomes moot once everything lives in one merged repo (no git-dependency indirection left), but until/unless that happens, dropping this script breaks the whole dependency chain silently (the failure only surfaces as a missing-module error deep in the consumer's build).

observations.what: Pinned Node to 24.12.0 via .tool-versions (mise); build already worked cleanly on it.
observations.why_it_matters: Build-only convenience, matches the same pin applied in the other two forks. Nothing breaks at runtime if dropped.

observations.what: appHasMonthlyNotesPluginLoaded, appHasQuarterlyNotesPluginLoaded, and appHasYearlyNotesPluginLoaded still inlined app.plugins.getPlugin('periodic-notes') directly, missing the dev-id fallback that be90253 had already applied to the daily/weekly checks -- so with only a dev-id Periodic Notes build installed, monthly/quarterly/yearly note-availability detection wrongly reported the plugin as unavailable. Now export and reuse getPeriodicNotesPlugin() from settings.ts in all three.
observations.why_it_matters: Same class of bug as be90253, but for three more granularities that be90253 missed. A merge that ports be90253 but not this follow-up commit reintroduces this exact gap for monthly/quarterly/yearly notes.

observations.what: obsidian-calendar-plugin re-implements the dev-id-then-store-id plugin lookup inline in its own src/settings.ts (appHasPeriodicNotesPluginLoaded, getMonthlyNotesPeriodicNotesPlugin) instead of importing daily-notes-interface's now-exported getPeriodicNotesPlugin() (public since bba664e), even though obsidian-calendar-plugin already depends on obsidian-daily-notes-interface directly.
observations.why_it_matters: Three independent copies of the same hardcoded 'periodic-notes-anks' id now exist across the two forks. A merge should consolidate to one; otherwise a future rename of the dev-build id has to be applied correctly in three places instead of one, and it's easy to miss one (as bba664e itself demonstrates happened once already).

observations.what: The obsidian-calendar-ui dependency actually built into obsidian-calendar-plugin is the published npm package version 0.3.12 (resolved from registry.yarnpkg.com per yarn.lock), NOT the locally checked-out /Users/anna.nowak/projects/obsidian/obsidian-calendar-ui repo. That local checkout's package.json reports version 0.4.0, and its HEAD commit message ('Fixes for 2.0-beta.2 ...') indicates a later, unreleased development line. The local checkout carries no local (anks) commits -- HEAD equals origin/master exactly -- so it is faithful to liamcain's own repo, but it is a different, newer version of the code than what the plugin actually consumes at build time.
observations.why_it_matters: An agent porting 'what obsidian-calendar-ui does' by reading the local checkout will describe UI behavior (0.4.0 / 2.0-beta.2, e.g. its 'properly unload UI and eventlisteners' and month-metadata-refresh fixes) that is not what is actually bundled into the plugin today (0.3.12). The merge must explicitly decide which calendar-ui version's behavior to carry forward, since the two are not the same code and the newer one was never actually wired in.

observations.what: obsidian-calendar-ui carries no fork-local modifications: HEAD (c275987) is byte-identical to origin/master, and its only configured remote, 'origin', already points at liamcain/obsidian-calendar-ui -- there is no separate matisnape fork or 'upstream' remote for this repo. git status and git stash list are both empty.
observations.why_it_matters: Confirms this repo needs no divergence-preservation work of its own during the merge; the only thing that matters from it is the version-pin mismatch captured in the observation above.

observations.what: All four repos (obsidian-calendar-plugin, obsidian-periodic-notes, obsidian-daily-notes-interface, obsidian-calendar-ui) have completely clean working trees ('git status --porcelain' empty) and empty stash lists ('git stash list' empty) as of the analysis date.
observations.why_it_matters: Confirms this observation list is complete relative to on-disk state: nothing is sitting uncommitted or stashed that would be silently lost on top of what the commit history already captures.

observations.what: obsidian-calendaric defines the Granularity type three times, independently.
observations.why_it_matters: Widening the type to month/quarter/year means editing three places, and settings.ts already splits it into ActiveGranularity vs Granularity while the other two do not. A partial widening compiles and fails at runtime.

observations.what: The hardcoded dev plugin ids appear at six call sites across four functions in two repos, not three as first reported.
observations.why_it_matters: The merged plugin has one id, so every one of these probes must be deleted or repointed. Missing one leaves a lookup that silently resolves to null.

observations.what: appHasPeriodicNotesPluginLoaded() reads periodicNotes.settings?.weekly?.enabled — the same Svelte-store-as-plain-object bug that commit 39040cd fixed for the monthly path, compounded by 'weekly' being a key Periodic Notes no longer stores.
observations.why_it_matters: It always returns falsy, so the Calendar plugin keeps rendering its own Weekly Note Settings section instead of deferring to Periodic Notes. This is live in the vault today, not only a merge concern.

observations.what: A prefix-matched note is indexed but cannot be looked up. resolve() stores an entry with matchData.exact false when the strict parse fails and the loose one succeeds, but getPeriodicNote() returns only entries with matchData.exact === true.
observations.why_it_matters: This is live in the vault: week format gggg-[W]ww with allowPrefixMatch on, and 60 weekly files named 'YYYY-Wnn, DD.MM - DD.MM.md'. Opening such a week finds nothing and creates a second, raw-named file next to the existing one. Prefix matching is only half-wired, so the rewrite must carry the match through lookup and open, not only through indexing.
